message.content: <local-command-caveat>Caveat: The messages below were generated by the user while running local commands. DO NOT respond to these messages or otherwise consider them in your response unless the user explicitly asks you to.</local-command-caveat>

<local-command-stdout>Set effort level to max (this session only): Maximum capability with deepest reasoning. May use excessive tokens resulting in long response times or overthinking. Use sparingly for the hardest tasks.</local-command-stdout>

addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.content:
1	# andesim-demo test roadmap
2	
3	Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
4	its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.
5	
6	Conventions (same as the existing demos):
7	
8	- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
9	  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
10	- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
11	  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
12	- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
13	  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
14	- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
15	  fast-only; each entry says which).
16	
17	Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
18	coverage today.
19	
20	---
21	
22	## 1. hotloops
23	
24	State: TODO
25	Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.
26	
27	Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
28	checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
29	runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
30	names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
31	`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
32	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
33	output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.
34	
35	- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
36	- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
37	  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
38	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.
39	
40	## 2. verify
41	
42	State: DONE
43	Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).
44	
45	Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math under
46	RTZ, a strip-mined RVV loop, CSR writes staged before AND inside the ROI)
47	runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
48	exit and compares the drained state field by field against the cycle
49	engine. Two builds from one source: `verify.elf` must PASS; the teeth are
50	`verify_taint.elf`, identical except one instruction sampling `mcycle`
51	into `t6` at the exit marker -- engine-divergent by design, so verify
52	must FAIL, name exactly `x31`, and exit non-zero. In the sweep the demo
53	is V-gated (`NEED_V`): the kernel uses RVV intrinsics.
54	
55	- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
56	- Pass: check.sh asserts `[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
57	  matches the QEMU oracle` on the clean build, and rc!=0 +
58	  `[state-diff] x31:` + `FAIL: 1 mismatch` on the taint build.
59	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.
60	
61	## 3. kanata
62	
63	State: TODO
64	Modes: hybrid only.
65	
66	See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
67	`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
68	with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
69	well-formed without a GUI.
70	
71	- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
72	- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
73	  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
74	  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
75	- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
76	  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
77	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.
78	
79	## 4. engines
80	
81	State: DONE
82	Modes: the whole suite, once per installed vsim engine.
83	
84	One suite, N cores - design-space switching, not a new demo dir. Every
85	demo's cycle/hybrid target already takes `ENGINE=<id>`, so the deliverable
86	is the sweep: `make check-all-engines` runs the aggregate `check` once per
87	vsim engine parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (restrict with
88	`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a ..."`) and prints a per-engine OK/FAILED summary.
89	Demos are capability-gated per engine from the driver's own output: the
90	lm*/hvm* demos skip when the engine's resolved hybrid plan (`--dry-run`)
91	carries no ILM/DLM/HVM sidecar args (`ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and rvv
92	skips when the engine's `list engines` row shows no VLEN.
93	
94	- Key files: top `Makefile` (`check-all-engines`), `README.md`
95	- Pass: `make check-all-engines` exits 0. Teeth: a bogus engine in
96	  SWEEP_ENGINES makes the sweep report FAILED and exit nonzero.
97	- Deps: none.
98	
99	## 5. fp
100	
101	State: DONE
102	Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
103	
104	Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
105	integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
106	RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
107	rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
108	expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
109	`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.
110	
111	- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
112	- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
113	- Deps: none.
114	
115	## 6. cache
116	
117	State: DONE
118	Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.
119	
120	Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
121	one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
122	`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
123	runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
124	larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
125	disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.
126	
127	- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
128	- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
129	  factor once real numbers exist).
130	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
131	  timing rides along").
132	
133	### 6b. cache: L2C/L3C MMIO transport leg
134	
135	State: DONE (2026-07-15)
136	Modes: hybrid only (marker) -- fast never leaves QEMU's stub, cycle never
137	leaves the RTL; only hybrid crosses the boundary under test.
138	
139	Prove the platform shared-cache registers at 0xE0500000 ride the handoff:
140	the QEMU leg stages Control policy bits (RMW), HPM Control 0 and
141	WAYMASK0-4; the vsim ROI reads them back FROM THE RTL and prints
142	`L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK` before the exit marker. Separate tests per cache level
143	(one source, `-DSHC_L3`): the block is the L2C on 45-series engines, the
144	L3C on 46/66. Engine-gated by the `list engines` CACHE column (from
145	`--describe shared_cache_*`, which the vsim gate derives from the RTL's
146	`NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`). RO registers (Configuration, INITSTATUS)
147	and side-effect registers (CCTL command, W1C error) are excluded by
148	design. Passes on ax66_makatau (live 512K L3C); SKIPs naming the RTL
149	config on ax45mpv_premium/ax46mpv_advanced (built size 0). Companion
150	changes: vsim gate extension + Control policy-bit merge + describe keys;
151	driver descriptor/plan `l2c_base=`/verify mask/CACHE column.
152	
153	- Key files: `demo/cache/{l2c.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, `README.md`;
154	  vsim_andesim `src/hybrid/{shared_cache_config.hpp,resume_driver.hpp}`,
155	  `src/{simulator.hpp,main.cpp}`; andesim
156	  `driver/{engine_descriptor.hpp,run_plan.cpp,state_diff.cpp,cmd_list.cpp}`;
157	  ABI `hybrid/state_abi.h` (`HYBRID_L2C_CTRL_POLICY_MASK`).
158	- Pass: `make check-cache ENGINE=vsim:ax66_makatau` prints
159	  `[PASS] hybrid L3C transport (L3:512K)`; ax45/ax46 print the
160	  RTL-config SKIP.
161	- Deps: none.
162	
163	## 7. roi_rules
164	
165	State: TODO
166	Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.
167	
168	Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
169	is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
170	the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
171	cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
172	hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
173	the marker span.
174	
175	- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
176	- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
177	- Deps: none.
178	
179	## 8. diagnose
180	
181	State: TODO
182	Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).
183	
184	The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
185	`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
186	the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
187	line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
188	file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
189	(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
190	exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
191	quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
192	timeout).
193	
194	- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
195	- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
196	- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.
197	
198	## 9. rv32
199	
200	State: TODO
201	Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).
202	
203	The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
204	`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
205	no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.
206	
207	- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
208	- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or
209	  `--dry-run`) shows qemu32 was selected.
210	- Deps: needs an rv32-capable compiler (separate riscv32 gcc or multilib);
211	  the Makefile must skip with a clear message if the toolchain cannot do
212	  rv32.
213	
214	## 10. gdb
215	
216	State: TODO
217	Modes: fast first; cycle as a stretch goal.
218	
219	Attach a debugger, scripted. fast: launch `--gdb` in the background, drive
220	`gdb-multiarch` in batch mode (`-ex 'target remote :1234'`, break at a
221	symbol, continue, print a variable, kill). cycle: needs `$ICEMAN` pointing
222	at an OpenOCD 0.12+ wrapper speaking remote_bitbang (the Andes-bundled
223	0.10 has a known bug against this DTM) - build only if the host has it.
224	
225	- Key files: `demo/gdb/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
226	- Pass: the gdb batch log shows the breakpoint hit and the expected
227	  variable value. check.sh skips (with a message) when gdb/OpenOCD are
228	  missing.
229	- Deps: none in-repo; host tools required. Build last.
230	
231	## 11. priv
232	
233	State: BLOCKED (engine not installed)
234	Modes: hybrid.
235	
236	S/U-mode handoff: drop privilege before the ROI, prove the level and the
237	PMP mirror crossed. Requires the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired

# andesim-demo test roadmap

Each entry is one independent demo. One session builds ONE demo, then flips
its State and commits. States: `TODO`, `IN PROGRESS`, `DONE`, `BLOCKED`.

Conventions (same as the existing demos):

- Layout: `demo/<name>/main.c` + `demo/<name>/Makefile`; host-side checks go
  in `demo/<name>/check.sh` (the `memsize` precedent).
- Top-level `Makefile` gets `run-<name>` and the per-mode targets; `README.md`
  gets a short section describing what the demo proves.
- Pass signal: either the guest prints `<NAME>_OK` from inside the ROI, or
  `check.sh` asserts on the driver's output. Every demo must fail loudly.
- Demos run on every mode where the feature exists (some are hybrid-only or
  fast-only; each entry says which).

Priority = file order. 1-3 are headline USER_GUIDE features with zero demo
coverage today.

---

## 1. hotloops

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (pc trigger); the detector itself runs fast.

Measure a binary you cannot edit. `main.c` has one known hot loop (a
checksum over an array, >=10 iterations) and NO ROI markers. `check.sh`
runs `$(ANDESIM)/build/hotloops --min-iters 10 <elf>`, asserts the report
names the hot function, extracts the ready `measure:` line (a
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair), and pastes it into
`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger pc ...`. Closed loop: the detector's
output feeds the measurement command with no human guessing.

- Key files: `demo/hotloops/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh sees the hot function in the hotloops report AND a
  `[andesim] N cycles` line from the hybrid run using the reported PCs.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 4.3, docs/hotloops.md.

## 2. verify

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid only (marker trigger).

Trust the figure. A state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP math under
RTZ, a strip-mined RVV loop, CSR writes staged before AND inside the ROI)
runs with `--verify`: andesim re-runs the ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI
exit and compares the drained state field by field against the cycle
engine. Two builds from one source: `verify.elf` must PASS; the teeth are
`verify_taint.elf`, identical except one instruction sampling `mcycle`
into `t6` at the exit marker -- engine-divergent by design, so verify
must FAIL, name exactly `x31`, and exit non-zero. In the sweep the demo
is V-gated (`NEED_V`): the kernel uses RVV intrinsics.

- Key files: `demo/verify/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS: vsim drain
  matches the QEMU oracle` on the clean build, and rc!=0 +
  `[state-diff] x31:` + `FAIL: 1 mismatch` on the taint build.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.7.

## 3. kanata

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid only.

See the pipeline of exactly the ROI. A small kernel runs with
`--kanata roi.kanata --objdump kernel.S` (the dump generated at build time
with `objdump -d`). Users open the file in Konata; check.sh proves it is
well-formed without a GUI.

- Key files: `demo/kanata/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts the Kanata header line, that a known kernel
  mnemonic from the objdump is embedded, and the trace is non-trivial
  (more than a handful of retired instructions).
- Constraint to demo: marker mode needs exactly ONE exit marker in the ELF
  (more -> andesim errors and points at `--trigger pc`).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.8.

## 4. engines

State: DONE
Modes: the whole suite, once per installed vsim engine.

One suite, N cores - design-space switching, not a new demo dir. Every
demo's cycle/hybrid target already takes `ENGINE=<id>`, so the deliverable
is the sweep: `make check-all-engines` runs the aggregate `check` once per
vsim engine parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (restrict with
`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a ..."`) and prints a per-engine OK/FAILED summary.
Demos are capability-gated per engine from the driver's own output: the
lm*/hvm* demos skip when the engine's resolved hybrid plan (`--dry-run`)
carries no ILM/DLM/HVM sidecar args (`ax46mpv_advanced` has none), and rvv
skips when the engine's `list engines` row shows no VLEN.

- Key files: top `Makefile` (`check-all-engines`), `README.md`
- Pass: `make check-all-engines` exits 0. Teeth: a bogus engine in
  SWEEP_ENGINES makes the sweep report FAILED and exit nonzero.
- Deps: none.

## 5. fp

State: DONE
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).

Scalar FP state transport - fills the coverage gap next to `rvv` (which is
integer-V only). The QEMU phase sets a non-default rounding mode (`frm` =
RTZ) and raises a sticky `fflags` bit; the vsim ROI computes a
rounding-mode-sensitive result and checks: the result matches
expected-for-RTZ, and the pre-ROI sticky flag is still set. Proves
`fcsr` (+ `mstatus.FS`) crossed the handoff.

- Key files: `demo/fp/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest prints `FP_OK`.
- Deps: none.

## 6. cache

State: DONE
Modes: hybrid (marker), two variants of one source.

Why timing-config transport matters. The same kernel is built twice from
one `main.c`: variant A keeps crt0's cache enable (transported
`mcache_ctl`), variant B writes `mcache_ctl = 0` before the ROI. check.sh
runs both hybrid measurements and asserts the uncached figure is much
larger. Doubles as a write-mask demo: the restore carries variant B's
disable only because the program itself wrote the CSR.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(off) > 2 * cycles(on)` (calibrate the
  factor once real numbers exist).
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE section 6 ("Config that matters for
  timing rides along").

### 6b. cache: L2C/L3C MMIO transport leg

State: DONE (2026-07-15)
Modes: hybrid only (marker) -- fast never leaves QEMU's stub, cycle never
leaves the RTL; only hybrid crosses the boundary under test.

Prove the platform shared-cache registers at 0xE0500000 ride the handoff:
the QEMU leg stages Control policy bits (RMW), HPM Control 0 and
WAYMASK0-4; the vsim ROI reads them back FROM THE RTL and prints
`L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK` before the exit marker. Separate tests per cache level
(one source, `-DSHC_L3`): the block is the L2C on 45-series engines, the
L3C on 46/66. Engine-gated by the `list engines` CACHE column (from
`--describe shared_cache_*`, which the vsim gate derives from the RTL's
`NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB`). RO registers (Configuration, INITSTATUS)
and side-effect registers (CCTL command, W1C error) are excluded by
design. Passes on ax66_makatau (live 512K L3C); SKIPs naming the RTL
config on ax45mpv_premium/ax46mpv_advanced (built size 0). Companion
changes: vsim gate extension + Control policy-bit merge + describe keys;
driver descriptor/plan `l2c_base=`/verify mask/CACHE column.

- Key files: `demo/cache/{l2c.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, `README.md`;
  vsim_andesim `src/hybrid/{shared_cache_config.hpp,resume_driver.hpp}`,
  `src/{simulator.hpp,main.cpp}`; andesim
  `driver/{engine_descriptor.hpp,run_plan.cpp,state_diff.cpp,cmd_list.cpp}`;
  ABI `hybrid/state_abi.h` (`HYBRID_L2C_CTRL_POLICY_MASK`).
- Pass: `make check-cache ENGINE=vsim:ax66_makatau` prints
  `[PASS] hybrid L3C transport (L3:512K)`; ax45/ax46 print the
  RTL-config SKIP.
- Deps: none.

## 7. roi_rules

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (marker + pc) vs cycle as the reference.

Trigger semantics and measurement hygiene, executable. A `noinline` kernel
is called 3 times; both triggers are one-shot, so the measured window is
the FIRST call only. check.sh asserts the hybrid figure is far below the
cycle-mode total (which contains all 3 calls + boot). The source shows the
hygiene rule from USER_GUIDE 4.2: anchor the kernel through memory inside
the marker span.

- Key files: `demo/roi_rules/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: check.sh asserts `cycles(hybrid) < cycles(cycle) / 3`.
- Deps: none.

## 8. diagnose

State: TODO
Modes: hybrid (driver features, no new guest code needed - reuse the hello ELF).

The debugging workflow as a script. check.sh exercises, in order:
`--dry-run` (asserts 2 resolved command lines), `--print-memmap` (asserts
the DRAM/V-scratch rows), `--log-level 1` (asserts the `[andesim] mmap`
line), `--log-file` (asserts timestamped, level-tagged lines land in the
file), and one forced leg failure that must leave a repro bundle
(`[andesim] repro: kept run artifacts at ...` -> assert `manifest.txt`
exists there). Open point for the build session: pick the most reliable
quick failure (candidate: a `--pc-end` that never retires, with a short
timeout).

- Key files: `demo/diagnose/{Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: every assertion in check.sh.
- Deps: none. Reference: USER_GUIDE 5.5, 5.6, 5.10, 8.

## 9. rv32

State: TODO
Modes: fast only (no rv32 cycle engine installed; hybrid rejects rv32 by design).

The rv32 runtime flavor and engine auto-select. Build hello against
`build/runtime/rv32` (`-march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d`), run `--mode fast` with
no `--engine`, and show the driver picked `qemu32` from the ELF width.

- Key files: `demo/rv32/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: hello output + exit code propagated; `--log-level 1` (or
  `--dry-run`) shows qemu32 was selected.
- Deps: needs an rv32-capable compiler (separate riscv32 gcc or multilib);
  the Makefile must skip with a clear message if the toolchain cannot do
  rv32.

## 10. gdb

State: TODO
Modes: fast first; cycle as a stretch goal.

Attach a debugger, scripted. fast: launch `--gdb` in the background, drive
`gdb-multiarch` in batch mode (`-ex 'target remote :1234'`, break at a
symbol, continue, print a variable, kill). cycle: needs `$ICEMAN` pointing
at an OpenOCD 0.12+ wrapper speaking remote_bitbang (the Andes-bundled
0.10 has a known bug against this DTM) - build only if the host has it.

- Key files: `demo/gdb/{main.c,Makefile,check.sh}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: the gdb batch log shows the breakpoint hit and the expected
  variable value. check.sh skips (with a message) when gdb/OpenOCD are
  missing.
- Deps: none in-repo; host tools required. Build last.

## 11. priv

State: BLOCKED (engine not installed)
Modes: hybrid.

S/U-mode handoff: drop privilege before the ROI, prove the level and the
PMP mirror crossed. Requires the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired
with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66`; `./andesim list engines` currently shows only
the two M-mode-only engines. Unblock by installing that engine, then spec
the demo.

- Key files: `demo/priv/{main.c,Makefile}`, top `Makefile`, `README.md`
- Pass: guest running in S-mode (or U-mode) inside the ROI prints `PRIV_OK`.
- Deps: ax66_makatau engine install.

---

- Deps: vsim_andesim PLMT (then PLIC) model.

## Port study: no port needed / not portable

Already covered, no port:

- `hello`, `coremark`, `dhrystone`, `rvv`, `syscall` - direct equivalents
  in SUBDIRS (ours add ROI markers, any-VLEN strip-mining, the uncached
  SimControl syscall window).
- `lm_test`, `hvm_test` - covered by `lm`/`lm_slave`/`lm_dma` and
  `hvm_slave`/`hvm_dma`. The old demos filled the memories through a
  sim-control "custom master" backdoor (0xe0080000 = 0xabcdeX); ours use
  the real transports (hart-local view, bus slave aperture, ATCDMAC300).
- `platform/uart_demo` - every demo's printf already exercises UART2.
- `hybrid`, `savable_feat` - the driver's hybrid mode plus the `verify`
  demo ARE the save/restore story; the driver has no user-facing
  `--save`/`--resume`, and adding one is a driver feature, not a demo.

Not portable:

- `ace`, `ace-rvv` - need the COPILOT toolflow (`.eca` for the assembler)
  plus a csim model (`libaceasim.a`) baked into the simulator build, and
  QEMU cannot execute ACE custom instructions, so fast mode, hybrid
  staging and the `--verify` oracle all break by construction. ax66 RTL
  has `NDS_ACE_SUPPORT=no` (ax45/ax46 have `yes`, but the generated
  instructions must match what COPILOT put into the RTL).
- `acervv46quad` - sources missing upstream (its Makefile references
  absent `.ace`/`.c` files and a private GEN_API tool).

#=========================================================================
# crt0.S : Entry point for RISC-V user programs
#=========================================================================

#ifndef CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
#define CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS 0
#endif

#define mcache_ctl 0x7ca
#define mmisc_ctl 0x7d0

  .text
  .global _start
  .type   _start, @function
_start:
  # Enable icache
  csrsi   mcache_ctl, 0x1

#ifdef ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE
  # Enable dcache coherence management
  li      a0, 1 << 19
  csrs    mcache_ctl, a0
1:
  csrr    a0, mcache_ctl
#if __nds_v5
  bbc     a0, 20, 1b
#else
  srli    a1, a0, 20
  andi    a1, a1, 1
  beqz    a1, 1b
#endif
#endif

  # Enable d-cache and hardware prefetch
  ori     a0, a0, 0x703
  csrw    mcache_ctl, a0

  .weak   _stack
  # Initialize stack pointer (if defined)
  lla     a0, _stack
  beqz    a0, 1f
  mv      sp, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  slli    a0, a0, 12
  sub     sp, sp, a0
#endif

  # Initialize global pointer
.option push
.option norelax
1:lla gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop

#ifdef __nds_v5
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg
  bbc     a0, 3, 1f
  la      a1, _ITB_BASE_
  csrrw   x0, uitb, a1
1:
#if __riscv_xlen >= 64
  bbc     a0, 52, 1f
#else
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg2
  bbc     a0, 20, 1f
#endif
  csrr    a0, mrvarch_cfg
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  la      a0, __jvt_base$
  csrw    jvt, a0
#endif
1:

  # Set mstatus.fs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 13)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Set mstatus.vs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 10)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Enable unaligned memory access (mmisc_ctl.UNA)
  li      a0, (1 << 6)
  csrs    mmisc_ctl, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss

  li      a1, 0xa55a
.Lother_hart_wait_loop:
  ld      a0, other_hart_boot_flag
  bne     a0, a1, .Lother_hart_wait_loop
  j       .Lmain
#else
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss
  li      a0, 0x01234571
  li      a1, 0xe0080000
  sw      a0, 0(a1)
1:
  j       1b
#endif

  # Clear the bss segment
.Lclear_bss:
  la      a0, _edata
  la      a2, _end
  sub     a2, a2, a0
  li      a1, 0
  call    memset


#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  li      a0, 0xa55a
  lla     a1, other_hart_boot_flag
  sd      a0, 0(a1)
  fence
#endif

  call init_mtvec

.Lmain:
  li      a0, 0
  li      a1, 0
  li      a2, 0
  call    main

  call    _exit

.Lloop:
  j       .Lloop

  .size   _start, .-_start

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  .data
  .p2align 3
  .global other_hart_boot_flag
  .type   other_hart_boot_flag, @object
other_hart_boot_flag:
  .8byte 0
  .size other_hart_boot_flag, . - other_hart_boot_flag
#endif

	$(ANDESIM_BIN) --mode hybrid --trigger pc \
	    --pc-start fp_roi --pc-end fp_roi_end \
	    --engine $(ENGINE) $(ANDESIM_FLAGS) $<

run: fp-fast fp-cycle fp-hybrid-marker fp-hybrid-pc

clean:
	- rm -f fp.elf fp.dump

.PHONY: all run clean fp-fast fp-cycle fp-hybrid-marker fp-hybrid-pc

1	/* Unified linker script for all hybrid test fixtures.
2	 *
3	 * Load base: 0x00100000 (1 MiB into andes_ae350 DRAM).
4	 *
5	 * andes_ae350 memory map:
6	 *   DRAM : 0x00000000 .. 0x7FFFFFFF  (writable, executable)
7	 *   MROM : 0x80000000 .. 0x87FFFFFF  (read-only)
8	 *
9	 * Reserved scratch (below text, used by .S fixtures):
10	 *   0x00000004              rt_csr_survival mtvec test value
11	 *   0x00001000              semihost_exit.inc param block
12	 *   0x00002000              rt_all_gprs spill area
13	 *   0x00003000              rt_mem_loadstore / rt_unaligned_lh buffer
14	 *   0x00010000              rt_shared_mem 4 KB buffer
15	 *
16	 * Layout above 0x00100000:
17	 *   .text         pinned at 0x00100000 (entry _start)
18	 *   .rodata
19	 *   .data         _edata terminates .data
20	 *   .bss          _end   terminates .bss (crt0 zeros [.bss, _end))
21	 *   _stack        0x00700000 (used by crt0.S to init sp)
22	 *
23	 * V-register transport scratch (L26): NOT a fixed address any more. The driver
24	 * maps one 4 KiB page above --mem-size and parks the scratch there (the mmap's
25	 * top page, v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + --mem-size), so it sits just past the
26	 * program's RAM -- nothing in this script can collide with it. No reservation
27	 * needed here.
28	 *
29	 * .S fixtures with no .data/.bss leave those sections empty (zero cost).
30	 * C fixtures rely on _edata / _end / _stack.
31	 */
32	
33	ENTRY(_start)
34	
35	SECTIONS {
36	    . = 0x00100000;
37	
38	    .text : {
39	        *(.text.init)
40	        *(.text*)
41	    }
42	
43	    .rodata : {
44	        *(.rodata*)
45	        *(.srodata*)
46	    }
47	
48	    .data : {
49	        *(.data*)
50	        *(.sdata*)
51	    }
52	    _edata = .;
53	
54	    .bss : {
55	        *(.bss*)
56	        *(.sbss*)
57	        *(COMMON)
58	    }
59	    _end = .;
60	
61	    /* Default stack top; the V-transport scratch lives above program RAM
62	     * (top of the shared mmap), so no headroom below it is needed here.
63	     * Override at link time with -Wl,--defsym,_stack=... if needed. */
64	    PROVIDE(_stack = 0x00700000);
65	}
66

/* Unified linker script for all hybrid test fixtures.
 *
 * Load base: 0x00100000 (1 MiB into andes_ae350 DRAM).
 *
 * andes_ae350 memory map:
 *   DRAM : 0x00000000 .. 0x7FFFFFFF  (writable, executable)
 *   MROM : 0x80000000 .. 0x87FFFFFF  (read-only)
 *
 * Reserved scratch (below text, used by .S fixtures):
 *   0x00000004              rt_csr_survival mtvec test value
 *   0x00001000              semihost_exit.inc param block
 *   0x00002000              rt_all_gprs spill area
 *   0x00003000              rt_mem_loadstore / rt_unaligned_lh buffer
 *   0x00010000              rt_shared_mem 4 KB buffer
 *
 * Layout above 0x00100000:
 *   .text         pinned at 0x00100000 (entry _start)
 *   .rodata
 *   .data         _edata terminates .data
 *   .bss          _end   terminates .bss (crt0 zeros [.bss, _end))
 *   _stack        0x00700000 (used by crt0.S to init sp)
 *
 * V-register transport scratch (L26): NOT a fixed address any more. The driver
 * maps one 4 KiB page above --mem-size and parks the scratch there (the mmap's
 * top page, v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + --mem-size), so it sits just past the
 * program's RAM -- nothing in this script can collide with it. No reservation
 * needed here.
 *
 * .S fixtures with no .data/.bss leave those sections empty (zero cost).
 * C fixtures rely on _edata / _end / _stack.
 */

ENTRY(_start)

SECTIONS {
    . = 0x00100000;

    .text : {
        *(.text.init)
        *(.text*)
    }

    .rodata : {
        *(.rodata*)
        *(.srodata*)
    }

    .data : {
        *(.data*)
        *(.sdata*)
    }
    _edata = .;

    .bss : {
        *(.bss*)
        *(.sbss*)
        *(COMMON)
    }
    _end = .;

    /* Default stack top; the V-transport scratch lives above program RAM
     * (top of the shared mmap), so no headroom below it is needed here.
     * Override at link time with -Wl,--defsym,_stack=... if needed. */
    PROVIDE(_stack = 0x00700000);
}

1	# CLAUDE.md
2	
3	This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
4	* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.
5	
6	## Repository Overview
7	
8	Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).
9	
10	One Git submodule:
11	- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
12	  contract under `include/hybrid/`, pinned by andesim AND by the external vsim, so
13	  there is one source of truth.
14	
15	QEMU and vsim are NOT submodules -- both are prebuilt external binaries:
16	- QEMU: point `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your `qemu-system-*` build dir.
17	- vsim: point `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your external vsim `build/` dir (the
18	  `sim_*` binaries). The vsim sources -- including the vsim-side hybrid
19	  orchestration (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`), `CMakeLists.txt`, and `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`
20	  referenced throughout this doc -- live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo and are
21	  built there (its own `build_vsim.sh`), no longer nested under `verilator/` here.
22	
23	## Build Commands
24	
25	**Primary path (`./andesim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
26	first use), the only driver, used in all user-facing docs.
27	
28	```sh
29	bash scripts/build_all.sh        # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
30	bash scripts/test_all.sh         # unit + contract + e2e suite
31	./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] <elf>
32	./andesim profile [--engine ID] <elf>   # hot-loop detector (engine-synced QEMU; docs/profile.md)
33	./andesim list <models|engines>
34	```
35	
36	**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
37	working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:
38	
39	```sh
40	# Build everything (locate external qemu -> vsim -> plugin)
41	source ./setup.sh
42	
43	# QEMU and vsim are NOT built here -- both are prebuilt external binaries. Point
44	# config.env's QEMU_BIN_DIR at your qemu-system-* build dir and VSIM_BIN_DIR at
45	# your external vsim build/ dir (see config.env.example); setup.sh validates both
46	# and exports VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_BIN_DIR.
47	
48	# Build individual components (vsim is built in its own external checkout)
49	make -C qemu_plugin                        # TCG plugins (out-of-tree; vendored qemu-plugin.h, no QEMU source needed)
50	
51	# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
52	make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
53	make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture
54	
55	# Clean (vsim is external; not cleaned here)
56	source ./setup.sh clean [plugin|all]
57	```
58	
59	**Outputs:**
60	- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotIterationLoop.so`, the `andesim profile` plugin)
61	- the vsim `sim_*` binaries are produced in the external vsim checkout under
62	  `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`).
63	
64	QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries, not built here:
65	`$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64` and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in
66	`config.env`). The vsim repo's own `build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman): it
67	builds an image from its `Dockerfile` (target `env`), runs `./build.sh` inside,
68	and pins the shared ABI as a nested submodule at `external/andesim_abi`.
69	
70	## Running Tests
71	
72	```sh
73	# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
74	bash scripts/run_e2e.sh
75	
76	# Run with specific options
77	JOBS=4 MODE=marker bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, marker-mode only
78	JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
79	FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
80	LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory
81	
82	# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
83	# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
84	# To run ctest directly after build:
85	#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
86	```
87	
88	**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.
89	
90	`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.
91	
92	**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver's feature contracts. They run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).
93	
94	## Architecture
95	
96	### Two-Phase Handoff
97	
98	```
99	QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
100	```
101	
102	1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
103	2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
104	3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. The Program Buffer carries only state the abstract command space cannot reach: the V-data sweep, `vtype`+`vl` (Tier B, see V-State Transport below), and the L2C MMIO window. **Liveness gate**: restores whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value are skipped (a no-op write; each DM op costs ~200-900 simulated cycles). The reset baseline is drained once per (engine build, ELF) on the first hybrid run and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`; `--no-reset-baseline` disables. Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, the S/U PMP mirror. Verify-transparent by construction (skip only when the value is already there).
105	4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.
106	
107	**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The S/U trap CSRs `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are drained by the plugin since v1 and, since the ax66 registration (option A), restored + re-read + `--verify`-compared on S-mode-capable engines (caps gate SMODE; the describe list names them); on an M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) they stay drain-record-only. Other S-mode CSRs (`sstatus`, `sepc`, ...) remain deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.
108	
109	**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).
110	
111	### Trigger Modes
112	
113	The repo ships 2 switching modes (triggers); each measures one region you
114	choose. The C++ `andesim` driver exposes them via `--trigger marker|pc`.
115	
116	- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
117	- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.
118	
119	`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. The run yields a cycle figure: window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`).
120	
121	### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)
122	
123	`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.
124	
125	**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.
126	
127	**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.
128	
129	**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Flag clear (pre-v6 file) -> consumers fall back to restore/compare-everything.
130	
131	**Memory-content sidecars (NOT in `hybrid_state_v1`)**: ILM/DLM and HVM content travels OUTSIDE the state struct, as raw binary sidecar files next to each state file. The plugin (args `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size` in bytes; bases default `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000`/`0x90000000`) drains `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm` through the slave-port/subordinate apertures; the vsim leg backdoor-loads them (`--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` -- zero-sim-cycle Verilator hierarchical-reference pokes into the RTL SRAMs, NOT the DM Program Buffer); the exit drain dumps the read-duals next to the handoff-out state. Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.
132	
133	Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`, `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).
134	
135	### V-State Transport
136	
137	V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
138	L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
139	ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
140	maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
141	scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
142	program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
143	image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
144	required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
145	with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
146	Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
147	- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
148	  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
149	  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
150	- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
151	  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
152	  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).
153	
154	Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb), which also forces vstart=0;
155	with LMUL=8 one `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` moves a group of 8 registers, so all 32 move in
156	4 grouped ops in a single Program-Buffer execution. The scratch is packed at the
157	RUNTIME vlenb stride (`stage_v_to_scratch` drops the wire-format
158	`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` padding so each 8-register group is contiguous).
159	
160	V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
161	- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
162	- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)
163	
164	Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
165	1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
166	2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m8 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
167	   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
168	   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
169	3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
170	4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
171	5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
172	6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)
173	
174	`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
175	LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
176	sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.
177	
178	### Test Fixtures
179	
180	All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
181	sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
182	the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:
183	
184	| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
185	|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
186	| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
187	| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
188	| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 4; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |
189	
190	The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
191	then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.
192	
193	Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is inline in `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andesim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.
194	
195	## Key Files
196	
197	| File | Purpose |
198	|------|---------|
199	| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
200	| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
201	| `src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (vsim repo) | Phase dispatcher |
202	| `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (vsim repo) | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
203	| `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (vsim repo) | DMI state capture |
204	| `src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` (vsim repo) | V register transport via scratch region |
205	| `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` (vsim repo) | CTest registration for the hybrid doctest unit tests |
206	| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
207	| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |
