# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.
* Always update docs/USER_GUIDE.md if something changed.

## Repository Overview

Andes hybrid RISC-V simulator: QEMU 9.x (functional, MHz-level) + vsim (SystemC + Verilator, cycle-accurate) share architectural state across a magic-CSR boundary. The system runs a two-phase handoff: **QEMU1** (drain on CSR/PC trigger) -> **vsim** (resume + execute + drain). The cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` delta; there is no QEMU2 leg (the handback was removed).

One Git submodule:
- `include/` - the shared ABI (`andesim_abi` repo): the `hybrid_state_v1` wire
  contract under `include/hybrid/`, pinned by andesim AND by the external vsim, so
  there is one source of truth.

QEMU and vsim are NOT submodules -- both are prebuilt external binaries:
- QEMU: point `QEMU_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your `qemu-system-*` build dir.
- vsim: point `VSIM_BIN_DIR` (config.env) at your external vsim `build/` dir (the
  `sim_*` binaries). The vsim sources -- including the vsim-side hybrid
  orchestration (`src/hybrid/*.hpp`), `CMakeLists.txt`, and `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake`
  referenced throughout this doc -- live in the separate `hybrid_vsim` repo and are
  built there (its own `build_vsim.sh`), no longer nested under `verilator/` here.

## Build Commands

**Primary path (`./andesim`)** -- the end-user driver (C++, self-builds on
first use), the only driver, used in all user-facing docs.

```sh
bash scripts/build_all.sh        # builds qemu, vsim, plugin, fixtures
bash scripts/test_all.sh         # unit + contract + e2e suite
./andesim run --mode fast|cycle|hybrid [--trigger marker|pc] [--engine ID] <elf>
./andesim profile [--engine ID] <elf>   # hot-loop detector (engine-synced QEMU; docs/profile.md)
./andesim list <models|engines>
```

**Developer escape hatch** -- the underlying scripts. Use these when
working on the build system, the harness, or a single leg in isolation:

```sh
# Build everything (locate external qemu -> vsim -> plugin)
source ./setup.sh

# QEMU and vsim are NOT built here -- both are prebuilt external binaries. Point
# config.env's QEMU_BIN_DIR at your qemu-system-* build dir and VSIM_BIN_DIR at
# your external vsim build/ dir (see config.env.example); setup.sh validates both
# and exports VSIM_QEMU / VSIM_BIN_DIR.

# Build individual components (vsim is built in its own external checkout)
make -C qemu_plugin                        # TCG plugins (out-of-tree; vendored qemu-plugin.h, no QEMU source needed)

# Build RISC-V ELF test fixtures
make -C tests/fixtures              # all fixtures
make -C tests/fixtures rt_c_v_regs.elf  # single fixture

# Clean (vsim is external; not cleaned here)
source ./setup.sh clean [plugin|all]
```

**Outputs:**
- `qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so` (+ `libhotIterationLoop.so`, the `andesim profile` plugin)
- the vsim `sim_*` binaries are produced in the external vsim checkout under
  `$VSIM_BIN_DIR` (e.g. `/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/build/sim_ax45mpv_premium`).

QEMU and vsim are integrated as prebuilt external binaries, not built here:
`$QEMU_BIN_DIR/qemu-system-riscv64` and `$VSIM_BIN_DIR/sim_*` (set both in
`config.env`). The vsim repo's own `build_vsim.sh` is Docker-based (podman): it
builds an image from its `Dockerfile` (target `env`), runs `./build.sh` inside,
and pins the shared ABI as a nested submodule at `external/andesim_abi`.

## Running Tests

```sh
# All e2e tests in parallel (auto-detects job count from nproc + /dev/shm headroom)
bash scripts/run_e2e.sh

# Run with specific options
JOBS=4 MODE=marker bash scripts/run_e2e.sh         # 4-way parallel, marker-mode only
JOBS=1 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh                  # sequential (debug)
FILTER=rt_c_v bash scripts/run_e2e.sh           # regex filter on fixture name
LOG_DIR=/tmp/my-logs bash scripts/run_e2e.sh    # custom log directory

# Unit tests (inside vsim build container)
# The container build runs: cmake --build build -j
# To run ctest directly after build:
#   podman run ... ./build.sh && podman exec ... ctest --test-dir build -L hybrid-e2e
```

**Important:** on a high-core-count machine (128+ cores) `default_jobs()` computes `min(nproc, /dev/shm_free/256MB)` which can reach 128+. Running that many vsim Verilator processes simultaneously saturates CPU and causes timeouts. Use `JOBS=8` (or lower) as a practical cap: `JOBS=8 bash scripts/run_e2e.sh`.

`scripts/run_e2e.sh` exits 0 only when all tests pass. Logs go to a `mktemp` directory under `/tmp`; path is printed at the start of each run. Each test's full output lands in `$LOG_DIR/$mode--$name.log`.

**Manual driver tests**: `tests/andes_sim/test_andes_sim_*.sh` cover the C++ driver's feature contracts. They run manually during driver development, not wired into `scripts/run_e2e.sh`. Each script is self-contained (sources `setup.sh` artifacts, runs one subcommand, asserts on stdout). The same convention applies to `tests/plugin/test_plugin_*.sh` (QEMU-plugin-only smoke tests).

## Architecture

### Two-Phase Handoff

```
QEMU1 --(state file + shared mmap)--> vsim (resume + run ROI + drain)
```

1. **QEMU plugin** (`qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c`) - TCG plugin. On the marker trigger (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0`) or PC-trigger, drains QEMU's architectural state into a binary `hybrid_state_v1` struct written to `--outfile`.
2. **vsim handoff controller** (`src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp`) - Detects the trigger inside vsim, pauses the hart via DMI, then calls `ResumeDriver` to restore state.
3. **ResumeDriver** (`src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp`) - Writes GPRs/FPRs into the vsim hart via RISC-V Debug Module Abstract Commands, one write per register. Every CSR write -- the base M-mode scalars, the Andes V5 block, and the M-ext block -- also goes through Abstract Commands only, one write per CSR; there is no batched Program-Buffer sweep anywhere in the register/CSR transport, in either direction (a WARL/read-only CSR faulting mid-batch can't be tolerated the way the abstract path's per-CSR cmderr-clear can). `StateDrain` mirrors this: one abstract read per GPR/FPR/CSR. The Program Buffer carries only state the abstract command space cannot reach: the V-data sweep, `vtype`+`vl` (Tier B, see V-State Transport below), and the L2C MMIO window. **Liveness gate**: restores whose drained value equals the engine's own reset value are skipped (a no-op write; each DM op costs ~200-900 simulated cycles). The reset baseline is drained once per (engine build, ELF) on the first hybrid run and cached under `$XDG_CACHE_HOME/andesim/`; `--no-reset-baseline` disables. Never gated: mstatus, GPRs, dpc, dcsr, mcycle, minstret, the S/U PMP mirror. Verify-transparent by construction (skip only when the value is already there).
4. **StateDrain** (`src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp`) - On vsim exit trigger, reads back the full architectural state via DMI Abstract Commands into `hybrid_state_v1`. This is the end of the run: the cycle figure is the vsim `mcycle` minus QEMU1's drained `mcycle`. The old QEMU2 resume leg was removed entirely.

**CSR restore split**: `ResumeDriver` writes the CSRs the vsim phase can touch: `mstatus`, `mtvec`, `mscratch` (L23), `mepc`/`mcause`/`mtval`/`mie`/`mip` (L24), `mcycle`, `minstret`, `fcsr` (frm + sticky fflags, gated on `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`; L20), and the Andes machine-setup CSRs `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) + `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) (L21). The cache pair matters for the cycle figure, not correctness: crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via `mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional engine, so without transporting it vsim resumes at the ROI with caches at their reset default (disabled) and the whole window runs uncached -- inflating the cycle count severalfold. All are tolerant writes: an engine without a given custom CSR mirrors the write as a no-op. In the trap-free ROI these writable M-mode CSRs are ordinary read/write state, so they round-trip fully: restored at resume, re-read at drain (`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough`), and compared by `--verify` (`state_diff`). Two verify-side exceptions: `mip` is restored + re-read but NOT compared -- its pending bits are hardware/platform-driven (the timer bit tracks elapsed time, which advances differently in QEMU's functional clock vs vsim's cycle clock), so comparing it would false-positive; and `mtvec` is restored but not re-drained. The S/U trap CSRs `medeleg`/`mideleg`/`satp` are drained by the plugin since v1 and, since the ax66 registration (option A), restored + re-read + `--verify`-compared on S-mode-capable engines (caps gate SMODE; the describe list names them); on an M-only engine (`ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`) they stay drain-record-only. Other S-mode CSRs (`sstatus`, `sepc`, ...) remain deferred to the S/U-envelope work. The vsim phase is assumed trap-free, interrupt-free, and PMP-static; if a future workload needs traps or dynamic PMP inside the ROI, `ResumeDriver` must be extended.

**Privilege (L6)**: the handoff carries the real privilege level. The plugin drains the gdbstub `priv` register, `ResumeDriver` read-modify-writes `dcsr.prv` before `dret` (and verifies the write took -- an M-mode-only RTL like the default `ax45mpv_premium`, `NDS_NUM_PRIVILEGE_LEVELS=1`, WARL-pins the field, and the resume aborts with a pick-an-S/U-capable-engine error), and `StateDrain` reads `dcsr.prv` back at the exit halt. For S/U handoffs the producer's PMP block (64 `pmpaddr` + the 8 even `pmpcfg`) is also mirrored into the hart, because with PMP implemented and no matching entry every S/U access faults; M-mode handoffs keep PMP pass-through-only (L2). The `rt_priv_smode`/`rt_priv_umode` fixtures run on the S/U-capable `ax66_makatau` engine paired with QEMU `-cpu andes-ax66` (see `scripts/run_e2e.sh`); the ROI itself must still be trap-free, single-privilege, and paging-off (S-mode CSRs are not transported).

### Trigger Modes

The repo ships 2 switching modes (triggers); each measures one region you
choose. The C++ `andesim` driver exposes them via `--trigger marker|pc`.

- **marker mode** (default): Pattern-matches `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0` (entry) / `slti x0, x0, 0x5A1` (exit) at retire time. The markers are RISC-V HINTs (rd=x0 discards the result), i.e. architectural NOPs -- a marker binary also runs standalone on every engine and on silicon. Users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`).
- **PC mode**: explicit boundary PCs passed as `--pc-start S --pc-end E` (symbol name or `0x` address) resolved at startup; marker insns are bypassed. Both args are required.

`./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker|pc` is the unified orchestrator; `tests/e2e.sh` drives marker/pc internally. The run yields a cycle figure: window cycles = the vsim `mcycle` delta (`hybrid_state_v1::mcycle`).

### Shared ABI (`include/hybrid/state_abi.h`)

`hybrid_state_v1` is the binary wire format exchanged between the QEMU plugin and vsim. It holds: 32 GPRs, 32 FPRs, fcsr, M-mode CSRs (mstatus, mepc, etc.), PMP (64 pmpaddr + 16 pmpcfg), the V extension block (vstart, vtype, vl, vlenb, 32 vreg[], vxsat, vxrm, vcsr), (v3) the Andes V5 CSR block `struct hybrid_andes_csr andes`, (v4) the writable M-mode CSR block `struct hybrid_m_ext_csr m_ext`, and (v5) the L2C MMIO register window `struct hybrid_l2c l2c`. `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX=128` supports VLEN up to 1024 bits; the live width is the runtime `vlenb`, and a producer whose vlenb exceeds the ceiling refuses to drain instead of truncating (L11). Multi-byte fields are little-endian (native on RV64 + x86-64 host); the format is not endian-portable.

**v3 Andes block**: `struct hybrid_andes_csr` carries the Andes-specific CSRs a bare-metal Andes core sets up before the ROI -- 13 scalar CSRs (mxstatus, mpft_ctl, mclk_ctl, milmb, mdlmb, mecc_code, mhsp_ctl, msp_bound, msp_base, mcountermask_m, uitb, jvt, ucode) + PMA (pmacfg[2] @ 0xBC0/0xBC2, pmaaddr[16] @ 0xBD0..0xBDF). The 13 scalars are defined ONCE by the X-macro `HYBRID_ANDES_CSR_LIST(X)` in `state_abi.h`, which every consumer iterates (plugin drain, `ResumeDriver` restore, `StateDrain` re-read, driver `state_diff` verify) -- so adding a CSR is one line, no consumer drifts. Live only when `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES` is set (the plugin sets it when QEMU's gdbstub advertised at least one Andes CSR). All restores are tolerant (a core lacking the CSR no-ops the write); the block round-trips through the trap-free ROI and is `--verify`-compared, except `msp_bound`/`msp_base` (HW stack-protection bounds) and `milmb`/`mdlmb` (ILM/DLM base+enable) which are engine-reset-divergent -- QEMU resets `msp_bound`/`msp_base` to all-ones (a vsim core without HW stack protection drains 0), and drains the `milmb`/`mdlmb` enable bit clear while the vsim RTL drains it set -- so they are verify-excluded like `mip`.

**v5 L2C block**: `struct hybrid_l2c` carries the **L2 cache controller's MMIO register window** (`reg[]` = offsets 0x0000..0x0527, DS220 11.8.5 Table 112). Unlike every other block this is DEVICE MMIO, not a CSR: the plugin drains the whole window with `qemu_plugin_read_memory_hwaddr` (physical address `l2c_base`, default 0xE0500000), and `ResumeDriver::restore_l2c` writes back ONLY the writable boot-static config registers -- Control (0x0008: `CEN` enable + prefetch + ECC + RAM timing), HPM Control (0x0010), Way Allocation Masks (0x0300..0x0328) -- via Program-Buffer word stores (`sw`, per DS220 11.8.3's <8-byte access rule). The read-only Configuration Register, the side-effecting CCTL command registers (writing one re-issues an L2 cache op), and the W1C error registers are captured but never restored. `StateDrain::drain_l2c` re-reads the config registers (`lwu`) for `--verify` (`state_diff` compares `l2c.ctrl` with the RO INITSTATUS[14] bit masked). This is the MMIO analog of the `mcache_ctl` (L1-enable) transport, and matters for the cycle figure the same way: an L2-enabled engine that resumed with L2 disabled would run the ROI severalfold slower. **Restore is HARD-gated on the engine having an L2C** (`Simulator::l2c_present()` from `_NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB > 0`): a store to an absent L2C region faults the Program Buffer, unlike a tolerant CSR write. Every current engine is built `NDS_L2C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0`, so the block is transported forward-looking and the restore/drain no-op today. QEMU seeds the L2C Control Register's reset value (`CEN=1`, DS220 11.8.7) at machine init (`andes_ae350.c`), so a guest that relies on the default is not drained as `CEN=0`.

**v6 write-mask**: `write_mask[2]` (one bit per mask-governed config CSR, slot map + decode helpers in `include/hybrid/write_mask.h`, live under `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) records **which CSRs the guest actually WROTE** during the QEMU phase. The plugin decodes CSR-write instructions at translation time (`csrrw`/`csrrwi` always write; `csrrs/c` only when rs1!=x0; `csrrsi/ci` only when uimm!=0) and registers an exec callback only on instructions that write a mask-governed CSR -- steady-state code carries zero instrumentation, so the fast leg is unaffected. Consumers (`ResumeDriver` restore, `state_diff` verify) skip any governed CSR whose bit is clear: an untouched CSR's drained value is only QEMU's reset default, which can legitimately differ from the engine's RTL reset value (`msp_bound` all-ones vs 0, `milmb.IEN` 0 vs 1), so skipping keeps the engine at ITS OWN reset value -- what real silicon of that engine would hold -- and makes producer/engine reset divergence harmless by construction for every current and future engine, with no per-engine data in QEMU. Governed set: the v3 Andes scalars + PMA, the v4 M-ext block, `mcache_ctl`/`mmisc_ctl`. Never governed: GPRs/FPRs/V, mstatus, dpc/dcsr, counters, fcsr, the trap-writable CSRs (mepc/mcause/mtval/mip/mie -- hardware writes them without a CSR insn), mtvec/mscratch, and PMP (the S/U mirror is a correctness requirement). `ucode` is transport-always (DSP ops set its sticky OV flag without a CSR insn). Flag clear (pre-v6 file) -> consumers fall back to restore/compare-everything.

**Memory-content sidecars (NOT in `hybrid_state_v1`)**: ILM/DLM and HVM content travels OUTSIDE the state struct, as raw binary sidecar files next to each state file. The plugin (args `ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size` in bytes; bases default `0xA0000000`/`0xA0200000`/`0x90000000`) drains `<state>.ilm/.dlm/.hvm` through the slave-port/subordinate apertures; the vsim leg backdoor-loads them (`--ilm/--dlm/--hvm` -- zero-sim-cycle Verilator hierarchical-reference pokes into the RTL SRAMs, NOT the DM Program Buffer); the exit drain dumps the read-duals next to the handoff-out state. Armed by the engine's `--describe` sizes (`ilm_size`/`dlm_size`/`hvm_size`, bytes; 0 = no memory or wrapper lacks the set_*/get_* backdoor pair -- capability-gated so a config-has-it/wrapper-can't engine arms nothing). These QEMU memories are per-CPU overlays (LM) or standalone RAM (HVM), NOT backed by the shared mmap, so the sidecars are the only road their content travels; QEMU's raw geometry must be synced (`-readconfig` on the driver path, `-global` in tests/e2e.sh -- HVM's property is `hvm_size_pow_2`, log2) because QEMU's compiled-in defaults (2 MB ILM at 0x0, 1-BYTE HVM) are wrong for every engine.

Flags (`HYBRID_FLAG_RV64`, `HYBRID_FLAG_FP`, `HYBRID_FLAG_V`, `HYBRID_FLAG_ANDES`, `HYBRID_FLAG_M_EXT`, `HYBRID_FLAG_L2C`, `HYBRID_FLAG_WRITE_MASK`) gate which state blocks are live. The ABI struct is validated by `tests/hybrid/state_abi.test.cpp` (in the external vsim repo).

### V-State Transport

V data registers (v0..v31) move through a scratch region in the shared mmap.
L26: that region is the mmap's TOP page, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) =
ram_base + ram_size - HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`, NOT a fixed address. The driver
maps one page more than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp physical_mmap_bytes`), so the
scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size`, just above the program's RAM, where no
program layout can collide with it (`cmd_run` also rejects an ELF whose static
image would reach into it). `ResumeDriver`/`StateDrain` take the GPA as a
required-when-V argument (the simulator passes `v_scratch_gpa()`); a V handoff
with it unset throws. vsim drives the transfer via the Debug Module **Program
Buffer** while the hart is halted, so benchmark binaries issue no transport code:
- `stage_v_to_scratch` copies `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` into the scratch region
  before resume; `ResumeDriver` then sweeps `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch into the
  regfile (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=true).
- At drain, `StateDrain` sweeps `vse8.v v0..v31` from the regfile back to scratch
  (`pb_v_data_sweep`, load=false); `read_v_from_scratch` lifts the bytes into
  `hybrid_state_v1::vreg[]` (the drained handoff file; there is no QEMU2 ship step).

Each sweep leads with `vsetvl` to e8/m8 (vl=8*vlenb), which also forces vstart=0;
with LMUL=8 one `vle8.v`/`vse8.v` moves a group of 8 registers, so all 32 move in
4 grouped ops in a single Program-Buffer execution. The scratch is packed at the
RUNTIME vlenb stride (`stage_v_to_scratch` drops the wire-format
`HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX` padding so each 8-register group is contiguous).

V scalar CSR transport (vtype, vl, vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr):
- **Tier A** (Abstract Commands): vstart, vxsat, vxrm, vcsr, mstatus.VS
- **Tier B** (Program Buffer): vtype + vl via `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` (direct CSR write to vtype sets vill; vl is read-only; only `vsetvl` restores both atomically)

Restore order in `ResumeDriver::resume()` when `HYBRID_FLAG_V` is set:
1. `mstatus.VS` (enables V in the hart)
2. V-data reload sweep: `vsetvl` e8/m8 then `vle8.v v0..v31` from scratch in the
   Program Buffer. Runs BEFORE the architectural V-CSR restore (whose `vsetvl`
   overwrites the sweep's vtype/vl/vstart) and uses x5/x6/x7 as scratch.
3. `vsetvl x0, x5, x6` in Program Buffer (stages `vl` in x5, `vtype` in x6 via abstract GPR writes first)
4. `vstart` (AFTER vsetvl: vsetvl resets vstart to 0)
5. `vxsat`, `vxrm`, `vcsr`
6. GPR loop (overwrites the x5/x6/x7 scratch - safe now)

`StateDrain::drain_with_passthrough()` issues the matching `vse8.v` dump sweep
LAST, after every architectural read (GPRs/FPRs/V-CSRs/mcycle/minstret), so the
sweep's clobbers and any counter increments cannot corrupt the drained state.

### Test Fixtures

All fixtures run on the unified `tests/e2e.sh` harness, which
sets up an `/dev/shm`-backed shared mmap (128 MB) so memory survives
the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. Three fixture families:

| Family   | Examples                                                    | Notes |
|----------|-------------------------------------------------------------|-------|
| asm      | `handoff_roundtrip`, `rt_all_gprs`, `rt_csr_survival`, `rt_shared_mem` | no C runtime; don't strictly need shared mmap but use it anyway (~20 ms cost is negligible). |
| C-level  | `rt_c_hello`, `rt_c_matmul`, `rt_c_v_regs`, `rt_c_v_csrs`   | hybrid round-trip tests, linked through the vplat runtime (below). Shared mmap is REQUIRED -- vsim resumes on QEMU1's memory, so the stack/heap and `main()`'s frame must survive the QEMU1 -> vsim handoff. |
| vplat    | `vplat_hello`, `vplat_exit41`, `vplat_file`                 | smoke tests for the runtime's own features (exit code, file io). The runtime is engine-portable, shipped as `build/runtime/libandesim_runtime.a` (sources in `runtime/`; build with `make -C runtime` or `scripts/build_all.sh runtime`): UART stdio + SimControl exit + HTIF file io, NO semihosting -- the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid. Users link with `-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`. See docs/USER_GUIDE.md section 4; smoke tests in `tests/vplat/`. |

The shared mmap is created with `mktemp -p /dev/shm` + `truncate`,
then QEMU is launched with `-object memory-backend-file`.

Fixture source lives in `tests/fixtures/`; the shared runtime sources live at the repo root in `runtime/`. ALL C fixtures (rt_c_* and vplat_*) link through the shipped vplat runtime with the user command (`-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`); nothing in-tree links `-lgloss_vh` or uses semihosting syscalls anymore (asm fixtures still carry a semihosting exit fallback from `semihost_exit.inc`). V-using fixtures require `-march=rv64gcv`. Syscalls bottom out in MMIO devices both engines model (UART2 `0xf0300000`, SimControl/HTIF `0xe0080000` -- QEMU side is inline in `QEMU/hw/riscv/andes_ae350.c`), so a `printf` inside the ROI works on every engine (it just adds the real UART cycles to the figure); the old "Phase-2 no-syscall rule" survives only as a measurement-hygiene convention in cycle-measuring fixtures, and as a hard rule for user binaries that still link a semihosting libgloss. The ROI markers are HINT NOPs, so vplat binaries may carry them (`<andesim/ROI.h>`, installed to `build/runtime/include/`) and still run standalone on every engine; binaries you cannot edit delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead.

## Key Files

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` | Wire-format struct (shared by all three components) |
| `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` | TCG plugin: drain on trigger |
| `src/hybrid/handoff_controller.hpp` (vsim repo) | Phase dispatcher |
| `src/hybrid/resume_driver.hpp` (vsim repo) | DMI state restore (Tier A+B) |
| `src/hybrid/state_drain.hpp` (vsim repo) | DMI state capture |
| `src/hybrid/v_regfile_xfer.hpp` (vsim repo) | V register transport via scratch region |
| `cmake/HybridConfig.cmake` (vsim repo) | CTest registration for the hybrid doctest unit tests |
| `scripts/run_e2e.sh` | Parallel e2e runner (FIFO job pool, per-test logs) |
| `tests/fixtures/Makefile` | RISC-V ELF fixture build (Andes toolchain) |

RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ROI-marker portability contract (docs/archive/roi_markers.md F3): the markers shipped
# in <andesim/ROI.h> are RISC-V HINTs (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1), i.e.
# architectural NOPs. ONE marker binary must therefore
#
#   1. run to completion standalone on --mode fast  (the old csrwi 0x7C0
#      markers died here: 0x7C0 is MILMB on Andes cores, the exit marker
#      enabled ILM at base 0 and trapped forever),
#   2. run to completion standalone on the cycle engine,
#   3. hand off on --mode hybrid --trigger marker and print window_cycles.
#
# The same two-flag user command as F8; the header rides the -B prefix
# (gcc adds <prefix>/include to the include path).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"
GCC="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"

BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
RT="$ROOT/build/runtime"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"
[ -x "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64" ] \
  || fail "external qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"
[ -f "$ROOT/qemu_plugin/libhybrid_handoff.so" ] || fail "plugin not built"

make -C "$ROOT/runtime" >/dev/null || fail "runtime lib build failed"
[ -f "$RT/include/andesim/ROI.h" ] || fail "runtime did not install andesim/ROI.h"

TMP=$(mktemp -d)
trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
cat > "$TMP/roi.c" <<'EOF'
#include <andesim/ROI.h>
#include <stdio.h>

static volatile unsigned src[64], dst[64];

int main(void)
{
  printf("before roi\n");
  andesim_ROI_begin();
  for (unsigned i = 0; i < 64; i++)  /* memory-anchored kernel */
    dst[i] = src[i] + i;
  andesim_ROI_end();
  printf("after roi\n");
  return 0;
}
EOF

"$GCC" -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
  -B "$RT" -specs=andesim.specs "$TMP/roi.c" -o "$TMP/roi.elf" \
  || fail "two-flag build with <andesim/ROI.h> failed"

# The binary must embed exactly the published wire encodings.
OBJDUMP="$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
DIS=$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/roi.elf")
printf '%s\n' "$DIS" | awk '$2 == "5a002013"' | grep -q . \
  || fail "enter marker 0x5A002013 not found in disassembly"
printf '%s\n' "$DIS" | awk '$2 == "5a102013"' | grep -q . \
  || fail "exit marker 0x5A102013 not found in disassembly"

# 1. fast, standalone: markers are NOPs, program must finish.
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'before roi' || fail "fast: missing 'before roi': $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'after roi'  || fail "fast: missing 'after roi': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 2. cycle, standalone: same.
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'before roi' || fail "cycle: missing 'before roi': $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'after roi'  || fail "cycle: missing 'after roi': $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 3. hybrid, marker trigger: the same markers drive the handoff.
OUT=$(timeout 180 "$BIN" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
        --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium "$TMP/roi.elf" </dev/null 2>&1)
RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -Eq '^\[andesim\] [0-9]+ cycles$' \
  || fail "hybrid: missing cycle figure line: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "hybrid: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F1 contract: one ELF built against the vplat runtime (UART stdio +
# SimControl exit, NO libgloss_vh / semihosting) runs to completion on the
# cycle-accurate engine from reset: it prints via the modeled UART and
# terminates the simulation with exit code 0 via the SimControl write.
#
# This is the leg that is impossible with an -mvh build (vsim has no
# semihosting; see docs/archive/vsim_semihosting_investigation.md).
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.elf"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_hello.elf || fail "fixture build failed"

OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'hello from vplat' \
  || fail "cycle: missing 'hello from vplat' in: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# Nonzero exit code must propagate through vsim too.
make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_exit41.elf >/dev/null || fail "exit41 build failed"
timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_exit41.elf" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1
RC=$?
[ "$RC" -eq 41 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 41"

## 4. Prepare your own program

### 4.1 Compile once, run on every engine

Link against the andesim runtime and one ELF runs on `fast`, on `cycle`,
and across a `hybrid` handoff -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

- Use your Andes RISC-V GCC (the one `./andesim doctor` reports).
- `-B` points gcc at the runtime artifacts; use the absolute path when
  compiling outside the repo.
- `-specs=andesim.specs` swaps in the runtime's `crt0.o`, links
  `andesim.ld` (load base `0x00100000`), and pins the library order, so no
  semihosting library can leak into the link.
- Add `v` to `-march` (e.g. `rv64gcv`) for RVV code.

For rv32 targets use the rv32 compiler and the rv32 runtime flavor:

```sh
riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

Custom build system (no gcc driver)? Link the pieces directly:

```sh
... -nostartfiles -nodefaultlibs -T build/runtime/andesim.ld \
  build/runtime/crt0.o your_prog.o -L build/runtime \
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

What the runtime gives your program, on every engine:

| Channel          | Behavior                                                       |
|------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------|
| stdio (fd 0-2)   | `printf` etc. go to the simulator console (a modeled UART)     |
| exit code        | `exit(n)` (n < 256) terminates the simulation; `n` becomes the simulator process exit code |
| file io (fd > 2) | `open`/`read`/`write` pass through to host files, resolved against the engine's working directory |

A `printf` inside a measured ROI works -- but it adds the real UART cycles
to your figure. Keep measured kernels I/O-free when you want clean numbers.

### 4.2 Mark your region (ROI markers)

For `--trigger marker`, wrap the region you want to measure:

```c
#include <andesim/ROI.h>   /* shipped with the runtime; rides the -B flag */

andesim_ROI_begin();
my_kernel(a, b, c);
andesim_ROI_end();
```

The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (architectural NOPs), so a marker
binary also runs unchanged on `fast`, on `cycle`, and on real silicon.
Ship one binary; measure when you want.

> **Measurement hygiene:** keep the kernel anchored inside the marker span
> -- read its inputs and write its outputs through memory inside the span,
> or wrap the kernel in a `__attribute__((noinline))` function called
> between the markers. The markers pin memory I/O but not register-only
> compute, so a kernel that carries live values in registers across the
> boundary may be hoisted or sunk out of the measured window by the
> compiler.

### 4.3 Cannot edit the binary? Use PC boundaries

`--trigger pc` needs no markers: you name the window with `--pc-start` and
`--pc-end`, each a symbol name or a `0x` address (section 5.3). To find
the hot region of an unknown binary first, run the profile command:

```sh
./andesim profile --min-iters 10 my_kernel.elf
```

It runs the binary fast (QEMU, configured like your engine) and reports
the hottest loops (function, source line, PCs) with a ready `measure:`
line -- a `--pc-start`/`--pc-end` pair you can paste straight into the
hybrid command. See section 6 and `docs/profile.md` for the full flag
reference.

# Build tiny RV64 fixtures used by hybrid smoke tests.
#
# Toolchain location comes from the repo-root config.env (loaded by
# `source ./setup.sh`, which exports HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN). Override on the
# command line with `make TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain ...` if you want
# to bypass the env var.

TOOLCHAIN ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN)
# rv64 tools. The toolchain check is deferred to use-time (recursive `=` +
# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf

	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \

# $(error)), so a pure-rv32 `make rv32` -- which uses CC32/LD32 below -- needs
# only HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32, not HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN.
rv64_tc   = $(if $(strip $(TOOLCHAIN)),$(TOOLCHAIN),$(error HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN is not set. Run `source ./setup.sh` from the repo root, or pass TOOLCHAIN=/path/to/toolchain))
CC        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc
CXX       = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-g++
LD        = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-ld
OBJDUMP   = $(rv64_tc)/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump

# Runtime sources live at the repo root (runtime/) -- they are the
# user-facing andesim runtime; fixtures are just one consumer. The linker
# script moved with them (test.ld -> runtime/andesim.ld, same content).
RUNTIME_DIR := ../../runtime
LDSCRIPT    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld
# Fixture-only helpers (csr ROI markers; NOT part of the portable runtime).
HELPERS_DIR := runtime

CFLAGS  := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -nostdlib -static -Wall
LDFLAGS := -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static

# All fixtures share andesim.ld (load base 0x00100000, andes_ae350 DRAM).
RT_FIXTURES := rt_all_gprs rt_all_fprs rt_abi_aliases rt_sign_bits rt_pc_jump \
               rt_long_roi rt_mem_loadstore rt_unaligned_lh \
               rt_shared_mem rt_csr_survival rt_m_ext_counters \
               rt_m_ext_trigcause rt_priv_smode rt_priv_umode

# Attack / breakage programs: each demonstrates a bug in the hybrid handoff.
# NOT part of the standard 'all' target (they are expected to misbehave).
# Build individually: make break_vscratch.elf   (etc.)
BREAK_FIXTURES := break_vscratch break_vscratch_top break_mcycle_write \
                  break_verify_diverge

# C-level fixtures: standard newlib stdio (printf, fputs, ...) linked
# through the shipped vplat runtime (libandesim_runtime.a) with the
# same two-flag command users type (-B build/runtime
# -specs=andesim.specs), so the suites regression-test the real
# artifact. stdio goes out the ATCUART100 UART2 and exit/file-io through
# the SimControl device at 0xe0080000, all of which both QEMU's
# andes_ae350 and vsim model. No semihosting and no libgloss anywhere:
# vplat_syscalls.o in the archive provides every stub newlib needs, so
# the same ELF runs on fast, cycle AND hybrid and a syscall inside the
# ROI works (it just adds its real cycles to the figure).
RT_C_FIXTURES    := rt_c_hello rt_c_printf rt_c_matmul rt_c_static_buf \
                    rt_c_fcsr rt_c_dlm_data rt_c_ilm_code
RT_C_V_FIXTURES  := rt_c_v_regs rt_c_v_csrs rt_c_v_matmul rt_c_v_fill \
                    rt_c_hvm_data
RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES := vplat_hello vplat_exit41 vplat_file vplat_gettimeofday \
                       vplat_window

RUNTIME_SRCS    := $(RUNTIME_DIR)/crt0.S $(RUNTIME_DIR)/trap.S \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/handler.c
# Prereqs of the runtime grouped target(s) -- shared by the rv64 and rv32 rules.
RUNTIME_DEPS    := $(RUNTIME_SRCS) $(RUNTIME_DIR)/vplat_syscalls.c \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.ld $(RUNTIME_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                   $(RUNTIME_DIR)/ROI.h
VPLAT_RT_DIR := ../../build/runtime
VPLAT_RT     := $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/crt0.o \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                $(VPLAT_RT_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h
VPLAT_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall
# RVV-using fixtures need -march=rv64gcv; the runtime's rv64gc objects
# link cleanly into rv64gcv programs (ld unions the arch attributes).
# The crt0 already sets mstatus.VS to Initial, so V insns don't trap.
VPLAT_V_CFLAGS := -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 -Wall

# --- rv32 fixtures -----------------------------------------------------------
# A small rv32 set for the arch-match path; the bulk of the fixtures stay rv64.
# Built via `make rv32` (NOT part of `all`), only when HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 is set.
# rv32_c_hello reuses rt_c_hello.c (markers are arch-neutral HINTs); rv32_spin
# reuses spin.S. The rv32 runtime comes from build/runtime/rv32 (ARCH=rv32).
TOOLCHAIN32    ?= $(HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32)
CC32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc
LD32           := $(TOOLCHAIN32)/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-ld
CFLAGS32       := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -nostdlib -static -Wall
VPLAT_CFLAGS32 := -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 -Wall
VPLAT_RT32_DIR := ../../build/runtime/rv32
VPLAT_RT32     := $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/libandesim_runtime.a $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/crt0.o \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.ld $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/andesim.specs \
                  $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR)/include/andesim/ROI.h

.PHONY: all clean dump rv32

all: spin.elf handoff_roundtrip.elf \
     l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
     hvm_readback.elf \
     $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
     $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf \
     $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf)

# spin.elf: benign program at a mapped reset address; the engine-registration
# probe (tests/engines/probe_engine.sh, sim --probe) halts it mid-run via the
# DM. All targets share andesim.ld at 0x00100000.

spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c spin.S -o spin.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) spin.o -o $@

handoff_roundtrip.elf: handoff_roundtrip.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c handoff_roundtrip.S -o handoff_roundtrip.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) handoff_roundtrip.o -o $@

# Marker-drain probe fixtures: each writes a device / CSR / memory window,
# then hits the entry marker so the plugin drains. l2c_drain = the v5 L2C
# Control Register; wm_drain = a v6 mask-governed CSR; lm_drain = the ILM/DLM
# slave-port windows (LM transport F1).
l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.elf lm_drain.elf: %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@
lm_drain.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# LM transport (F2): reads back --ilm/--dlm content through the hart-local
# TCM view AND the slave-port aperture on the cycle engine (vplat runtime for
# the exit code).
lm_readback.elf: lm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h \
                 $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# HVM transport (F1, ROADMAP_hvm): reads back --hvm content through the
# 0x90000000 subordinate-port aperture on the cycle engine.
hvm_readback.elf: hvm_readback.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

$(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT) semihost_exit.inc
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# Break fixtures: same link as RT_FIXTURES but no semihost_exit.inc dependency
# (they exit via SimControl or deliberately hang).
$(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC) $(CFLAGS) -c $< -o $*.o
	$(LD) $(LDFLAGS) $*.o -o $@

# C-level fixtures: linked exactly like a user program (see VPLAT_RT
# above). rt_c_helpers.h rides -I$(HELPERS_DIR).
$(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# RVV-enabled fixtures: same link, different -march. Listed separately so
# changes to VPLAT_CFLAGS don't accidentally drop V.
$(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@
rt_c_hvm_data.elf: $(HELPERS_DIR)/memory_map.h

# vplat smoke fixtures (tests/vplat/): exercise the runtime's own
# features (exit code, file io) with no fixture helpers.
$(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf): %.elf: %.c $(VPLAT_RT)
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS) -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs $< -o $@

# One sub-make produces all five artifacts (grouped target, make >= 4.3).
$(VPLAT_RT) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR)

# Markerless GEMM twin. Explicit rule, NOT in RT_C_V_FIXTURES -- the
# pattern rule would look for a nonexistent rt_c_v_matmul_free.c. Same
# source, same link as the marked V fixtures, plus -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS
# (drops the ROI marker HINTs) so pc-mode and marker-mode measure the
# same GEMM kernel.
rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf: rt_c_v_matmul.c $(VPLAT_RT) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC) $(VPLAT_V_CFLAGS) -DHYBRID_MARKERLESS -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_v_matmul.c -o $@

# rv32 fixtures: one bare-asm (no runtime) + one C (links the rv32 runtime).
rv32: rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

rv32_spin.elf: spin.S $(LDSCRIPT)
	$(CC32) $(CFLAGS32) -c spin.S -o rv32_spin.o
	$(LD32) -T $(LDSCRIPT) -nostdlib -static rv32_spin.o -o $@

rv32_c_hello.elf: rt_c_hello.c $(VPLAT_RT32) $(HELPERS_DIR)/rt_c_helpers.h
	$(CC32) $(VPLAT_CFLAGS32) -I$(HELPERS_DIR) \
	  -B $(VPLAT_RT32_DIR) -specs=andesim.specs rt_c_hello.c -o $@

# rv32 runtime (grouped target): the runtime Makefile with ARCH=rv32.
$(VPLAT_RT32) &: $(RUNTIME_DEPS)
	$(MAKE) -C $(RUNTIME_DIR) ARCH=rv32 HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32=$(TOOLCHAIN32)

dump: spin.elf
	$(OBJDUMP) -d spin.elf

clean:
	rm -f spin.o spin.elf \
	      handoff_roundtrip.o handoff_roundtrip.elf \
	      l2c_drain.o l2c_drain.elf wm_drain.o wm_drain.elf \
	      lm_drain.o lm_drain.elf lm_readback.elf \
	      $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(RT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(RT_C_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) $(RT_C_V_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rt_c_v_matmul_free.elf $(RT_C_VPLAT_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.o) $(BREAK_FIXTURES:%=%.elf) \
	      rv32_spin.o rv32_spin.elf rv32_c_hello.elf

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# C++ contract: one g++-built ELF linked with the same two-flag command
# (-B build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs) runs on fast AND cycle, with
#
#   1. static constructors executed before main (crt0 ->
#      __libc_init_array -> .init_array; the fixture's ctor assembles the
#      "CPP" tag, so CPP_OK cannot print unless the ctor ran),
#   2. libstdc++ heap containers (std::string/std::vector) on _sbrk,
#   3. C++ return-from-main semantics: main's return routes through
#      exit(rc), so the static object's destructor prints CPP_DTOR_OK.
#
# The fixture exits 1 (CPP_FAIL...) on any miss, so both legs also assert
# the exit code.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

ELF="$ROOT/tests/fixtures/vplat_cpp.elf"
BIN="$ROOT/build/andesim"
SIM="$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium"
[ -x "$BIN" ] || fail "driver not built: $BIN"
[ -x "$SIM" ] || fail "cycle engine not found (source ./setup.sh): $SIM"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" vplat_cpp.elf || fail "g++ fixture build failed"

# 1. fast: ctor string + vector sum + dtor-at-exit.
OUT=$(timeout 60 "$BIN" run --mode fast "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'CPP_OK sum=10'      || fail "fast: missing CPP_OK: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'CPP_DTOR_OK tag=CPP' || fail "fast: missing CPP_DTOR_OK: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "fast: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

# 2. cycle: same contract from reset on the RTL engine.
OUT=$(timeout 120 "$SIM" "$ELF" </dev/null 2>&1); RC=$?
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'CPP_OK sum=10'      || fail "cycle: missing CPP_OK: $OUT"
printf '%s\n' "$OUT" | grep -q 'CPP_DTOR_OK tag=CPP' || fail "cycle: missing CPP_DTOR_OK: $OUT"
[ "$RC" -eq 0 ] || fail "cycle: exit code $RC != 0 (output: $OUT)"

/* Unified linker script for all hybrid test fixtures.
 *
 * Load base: 0x00100000 (1 MiB into andes_ae350 DRAM).
 *
 * andes_ae350 memory map:
 *   DRAM : 0x00000000 .. 0x7FFFFFFF  (writable, executable)
 *   MROM : 0x80000000 .. 0x87FFFFFF  (read-only)
 *
 * Reserved scratch (below text, used by .S fixtures):
 *   0x00000004              rt_csr_survival mtvec test value
 *   0x00001000              semihost_exit.inc param block
 *   0x00002000              rt_all_gprs spill area
 *   0x00003000              rt_mem_loadstore / rt_unaligned_lh buffer
 *   0x00010000              rt_shared_mem 4 KB buffer
 *
 * Layout above 0x00100000:
 *   .text         pinned at 0x00100000 (entry _start)
 *   .rodata
 *   .data         _edata terminates .data
 *   .bss          _end   terminates .bss (crt0 zeros [.bss, _end))
 *   _stack        0x00700000 (used by crt0.S to init sp)
 *
 * V-register transport scratch (L26): NOT a fixed address any more. The driver
 * maps one 4 KiB page above --mem-size and parks the scratch there (the mmap's
 * top page, v_scratch_gpa = ram_base + --mem-size), so it sits just past the
 * program's RAM -- nothing in this script can collide with it. No reservation
 * needed here.
 *
 * .S fixtures with no .data/.bss leave those sections empty (zero cost).
 * C fixtures rely on _edata / _end / _stack.
 */

ENTRY(_start)

SECTIONS {
    . = 0x00100000;

    .text : {
        *(.text.init)
        *(.text*)
    }

    .rodata : {
        *(.rodata*)
        *(.srodata*)
    }

    .data : {
        *(.data*)
        *(.sdata*)
    }
    _edata = .;

    .bss : {
        *(.bss*)
        *(.sbss*)
        *(COMMON)
    }
    _end = .;

    /* Default stack top; the V-transport scratch lives above program RAM
     * (top of the shared mmap), so no headroom below it is needed here.
     * Override at link time with -Wl,--defsym,_stack=... if needed. */
    PROVIDE(_stack = 0x00700000);
}

#=========================================================================
# crt0.S : Entry point for RISC-V user programs
#=========================================================================

#ifndef CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
#define CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS 0
#endif

#define mcache_ctl 0x7ca
#define mmisc_ctl 0x7d0

  .text
  .global _start
  .type   _start, @function
_start:
  # Enable icache
  csrsi   mcache_ctl, 0x1

#ifdef ENABLE_DCACHE_COHERENCE
  # Enable dcache coherence management
  li      a0, 1 << 19
  csrs    mcache_ctl, a0
1:
  csrr    a0, mcache_ctl
#if __nds_v5
  bbc     a0, 20, 1b
#else
  srli    a1, a0, 20
  andi    a1, a1, 1
  beqz    a1, 1b
#endif
#endif

  # Enable d-cache and hardware prefetch
  ori     a0, a0, 0x703
  csrw    mcache_ctl, a0

  .weak   _stack
  # Initialize stack pointer (if defined)
  lla     a0, _stack
  beqz    a0, 1f
  mv      sp, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  slli    a0, a0, 12
  sub     sp, sp, a0
#endif

  # Initialize global pointer
.option push
.option norelax
1:lla gp, __global_pointer$
.option pop

#ifdef __nds_v5
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg
  bbc     a0, 3, 1f
  la      a1, _ITB_BASE_
  csrrw   x0, uitb, a1
1:
#if __riscv_xlen >= 64
  bbc     a0, 52, 1f
#else
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  csrr    a0, mmsc_cfg2
  bbc     a0, 20, 1f
#endif
  csrr    a0, mrvarch_cfg
  bbc     a0, 31, 1f
  la      a0, __jvt_base$
  csrw    jvt, a0
#endif
1:

  # Set mstatus.fs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 13)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Set mstatus.vs to 1 (initial)
  li      a0, (1 << 10)
  csrs    mstatus, a0

  # Enable unaligned memory access (mmisc_ctl.UNA)
  li      a0, (1 << 6)
  csrs    mmisc_ctl, a0

#if CRT0_MULTIPLE_HARTS
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss

  li      a1, 0xa55a
.Lother_hart_wait_loop:
  ld      a0, other_hart_boot_flag
  bne     a0, a1, .Lother_hart_wait_loop
  j       .Lmain
#else
  csrr    a0, mhartid
  beqz    a0, .Lclear_bss
  li      a0, 0x01234571
  li      a1, 0xe0080000
  sw      a0, 0(a1)
1:
  j       1b
#endif

.Lclear_bss:
  la      a0, _edata
  la      a2, _end
  sub     a2, a2, a0
  li      a1, 0
  call    memset

  li      a1, 0
  li      a2, 0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# F6 contract: `scripts/run_e2e.sh` works out of the box -- its default
# VSIM_BIN must be the repo's canonical SINGLE-HART engine
# (sim_ax45mpv_premium, the same default ./andesim pins), NOT the
# alphabetically-first VSIM_BIN_DIR sim_* (sim_ax45mpv_mp2, a 2-core
# config where crt0's secondary-hart SKIPPED write stops the sim before
# hart 0 drains and every C fixture fails).
#
# The probe: one marker e2e fixture with NO VSIM_BIN in the environment.
set -uo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
. "$SCRIPT_DIR/../lib/log.sh"

# shellcheck disable=SC1091
. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null
export HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:?config.env missing}"

[ -x "$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_premium" ] || fail "premium engine not found (source ./setup.sh)"
[ -x "$(vsim_bin_dir)/sim_ax45mpv_mp2" ] \
  || echo "[note] mp2 engine absent; default-pick ambiguity not present on this host"
[ -x "${QEMU_BIN_DIR:-$(cfg_val QEMU_BIN_DIR)}/qemu-system-riscv64" ] || fail "qemu not found (source ./setup.sh)"

make -C "$ROOT/tests/fixtures" rt_c_hello.elf >/dev/null || fail "fixture build failed"

unset VSIM_BIN
FILTER='^rt_c_hello$' MODE=marker JOBS=1 bash "$ROOT/scripts/run_e2e.sh" \
  >/tmp/vplat_f6_run.log 2>&1 \
  || fail "default-engine e2e rt_c_hello[marker] failed (picked a multi-hart engine?): $(tail -4 /tmp/vplat_f6_run.log)"

C++ works through the same two flags -- just switch the driver to `g++`:

```sh
riscv64-unknown-elf-g++ -march=rv64gc -mabi=lp64d -O2 \
  -B <andesim>/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.cpp -o your_prog.elf
```

- Static constructors run before `main` (crt0 walks `.init_array` via
  newlib's `__libc_init_array`), and returning from `main` has C++
  `exit(rc)` semantics: atexit handlers and static destructors run.
- libstdc++ heap containers (`std::string`, `std::vector`, ...) sit on
  the runtime heap; the g++ driver adds `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, and the
  specs add `crtbegin/crtend`.
- Prefer `printf` over `<iostream>`: iostreams add hundreds of KB of
  code and static-init work that noticeably lengthens a cycle-mode boot.

```sh
  -Wl,--start-group -landesim_runtime -lc -lgcc -Wl,--end-group
```

(For C++, add `crtbegin.o`/`crtend.o` around your objects and `-lstdc++
-lm` before the group -- or just use the `g++` driver form above.)

feat(runtime): C++ support - .init_array ctors, dtors at exit, g++ link path (behavioral)

RED: tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh - a g++-built vplat_cpp.elf whose
static ctor assembles the pass tag failed with "CPP_FAIL static ctor
did not run": crt0 never walked .init_array and andesim.ld never
defined its bounds (newlib's weak __init_array_start/end resolved to
0, so __libc_init_array had nothing to walk even when called).

GREEN, smallest set that passes fast + cycle:
- andesim.ld: KEEP'd .preinit_array/.init_array/.fini_array with
  PROVIDE_HIDDEN bounds, plus .eh_frame/.gcc_except_table. Placed
  ABOVE _edata on purpose: crt0 zeroes [_edata, _end) before the
  walk, so arrays after .data would be wiped first.
- crt0.S: keep the direct init_mtvec call (the reference is what
  extracts handler.o+trap.o from the archive; trap vector is live
  before any ctor), then call __libc_init_array. main's return now
  routes through exit() - C++ requires return-from-main == exit(rc),
  so atexit handlers and static dtors run (asserted via CPP_DTOR_OK).
- andesim.specs: startfile/endfile gain crtbegin/crtend (__dso_handle,
  eh_frame begin/terminator), matching the upstream riscv-elf specs;
  the g++ driver injects -lstdc++ -lm itself, so *lib is unchanged.
- handler.c: drop the dead constructor attribute on init_mtvec (the
  walk would now run it a second time after crt0's direct call).

Regression: all 12 tests/vplat scripts pass (f6 needs `source
./setup.sh` for run_e2e's VSIM_QEMU - environmental, not new).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF
)" && git log --oneline -1
