content.content:
1	# andesim-demo
2	
3	Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
4	every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
5	(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).
6	
7	## Prerequisites
8	
9	- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
10	  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
11	- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).
12	
13	## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`
14	
15	Fill in these settings if your paths differ:
16	
17	```Makefile
18	ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
19	TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
20	ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
21	```
22	
23	## Step 2: Build
24	
25	```bash
26	make
27	```
28	
29	Each demo links against the andesim runtime
30	(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
31	runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.
32	
33	## Step 3: Run
34	
35	Run every mode of one demo:
36	
37	```bash
38	make run-hello
39	make run-lm
40	make run-lm_slave
41	make run-lm_dma
42	make run-hvm_slave
43	make run-hvm_dma
44	make run-rvv
45	make run-fp
46	make run-cache
47	make run-verify
48	make run-syscall
49	make run-coremark
50	make run-dhrystone
51	```
52	
53	Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
54	`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `verify-*`,
55	`syscall-*`, `coremark-*` and `dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):
56	
57	| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
58	|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
59	| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
60	| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
61	| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
62	| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |
63	
64	`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
65	QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
66	small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
67	outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
68	checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
69	On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
70	the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.
71	
72	`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
73	SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
74	DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
75	slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
76	(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
77	memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
78	engines and the content crossed the handoff.
79	
80	`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
81	controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
82	aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
83	ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
84	That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
85	models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
86	bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.
87	
88	The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
89	vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
90	enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
91	its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
92	demo:
93	
94	- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
95	  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
96	  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
97	  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
98	  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
99	- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
100	  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
101	  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.
102	
103	On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
104	each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
105	256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.
106	
107	`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
108	(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
109	workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
110	reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
111	compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
112	handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
113	`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
114	is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
115	vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
116	accepts it.
117	
118	`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
119	covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
120	rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
121	divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
122	`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
123	(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
124	`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
125	handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
126	sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
127	intact.
128	
129	`demo/cache` prices the config transport: the SAME kernel (4 passes
130	over a 1 KB volatile array) in two hybrid builds. `cache_on` is the
131	untouched program -- crt0 enables the L1 caches at boot, and only the
132	transported `mcache_ctl` makes the vsim ROI run cached, as this
133	program would on silicon. `cache_off` clears the IC|DC enable bits
134	before the ROI, so the transported value disables the caches and the
135	same window runs uncached -- about 4.5k vs 42.5k cycles, a ~9x gap on
136	this kernel (`make check-cache` asserts ratio > 2x). Without the
137	transport EVERY hybrid figure would look like `cache_off`: the engine
138	resets with caches off. The demo also carries the platform-cache MMIO
139	transport tests (`l2c.elf`/`l3c.elf`, one source): the program stages
140	patterns in the shared-cache registers (Control policy bits, HPM
141	Control, way masks) on the QEMU leg and asserts them back FROM THE RTL
142	inside the ROI, printing `L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK`. Hybrid-only by design, and
143	engine-gated: check.sh picks the leg matching the engine's CACHE
144	column (`L2:*` on 45-series, `L3:*` on 46/66) and SKIPs, naming the
145	RTL config, when it shows `-`. There is no cache_off cycle target on
146	purpose: disabling the D-cache mid-run on the RTL would strand its
147	dirty lines (that needs a CCTL flush first); on hybrid the vsim
148	caches start empty at the restore, so the plain disable is exact.
149	
150	`demo/verify` is about trusting the figure: `make verify-hybrid-marker`
151	runs a state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP under RTZ, an RVV
152	loop, CSR writes before and inside the ROI) with `--verify`, which
153	re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI exit and compares the
154	drained state field by field against the cycle engine
155	(`[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS`). The demo also shows the
156	failing side: `make verify-taint-hybrid-marker` runs a build whose only
157	difference is one instruction -- an `mcycle` sample into `t6` right at
158	the exit marker. The engines count cycles differently by design, so
159	that register cannot match: verify exits non-zero and the diff names
160	exactly `x31`. `make check-verify` asserts both directions.
161	
162	`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
163	binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
164	host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
165	and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
166	time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
167	runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
168	`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
169	also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
170	file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
171	files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
172	the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
173	hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
174	main's return value through SimControl).
175	
176	`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
177	sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
178	(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
179	functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
180	exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
181	That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
182	`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
183	same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
184	caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
185	gets the same window from the symbols alone
186	(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
187	`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
188	prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
189	figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
190	extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.
191	
192	`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
193	port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
194	the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
195	the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
196	`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
197	(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
198	same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
199	`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
200	default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
201	Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
202	second pass with `-DPASS2`).
203	
204	Expected output (hybrid):
205	
206	```
207	hello from andesim!
208	[andesim] 3532 cycles
209	```
210	
211	The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
212	close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.
213	
214	## Switching engines
215	
216	Every `cycle` and `hybrid` target takes its engine from the `ENGINE`
217	variable (default in `Make.var`), so any demo runs on any engine that
218	`andesim list engines` reports -- the binaries are engine-portable:
219	
220	```bash
221	make hello-hybrid-marker ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced
222	make check ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced        # the whole suite, one engine
223	make check-all-engines                          # the whole suite, EVERY vsim engine
224	```
225	
226	`check-all-engines` parses the engine set from `andesim list engines`
227	at run time (nothing hardcoded; restrict it with
228	`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b"`) and prints a per-engine summary.
229	Demos are capability-gated per engine: the local-memory demos
230	(`lm*`, `hvm*`) are skipped on an engine whose resolved plan carries
231	no ILM/DLM/HVM, and `rvv` is skipped on an engine without a vector
232	unit. The gate keys off the engine's `--describe` output, which
233	advertises LM *transport* (backdoor load + dump in the vsim CPU
234	wrapper) -- not whether the RTL config has the memories.
235	
236	### Demo x engine matrix (sweep of 2026-07-14)
237	
238	| Demo      | vsim:ax45mpv_premium | vsim:ax46mpv_advanced | vsim:ax66_makatau | Blocking layer for SKIP/FAIL |
239	|-----------|----------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|
240	| hello     | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
241	| lm        | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
242	| lm_slave  | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
243	| lm_dma    | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
244	| hvm_slave | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
245	| hvm_dma   | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
246	| rvv       | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
247	| fp        | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
248	| cache     | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
249	| cache/l2c+l3c | SKIP | SKIP | PASS (L3C) | RTL: ax45/ax46 built with `NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` (no shared-cache block); wrapper+driver transport ready |
250	| verify    | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
251	| syscall   | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
252	| coremark  | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
253	| dhrystone | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
254	| memsize   | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
255	
256	The cache/l2c+l3c row is the platform-cache MMIO transport leg inside
257	`make check-cache` (sweep of 2026-07-15). The shared cache is the L2C
258	on 45-series engines and the L3C on 46/66-series -- separate tests,
259	same registers: `l3c.elf` passes on ax66_makatau's live 512K L3C
260	(`andesim list engines` CACHE column `L3:512K`); ax45mpv_premium and

# andesim-demo

Demo programs for the `andesim` hybrid RISC-V simulator. One ELF runs on
every mode: `fast` (QEMU), `cycle` (vsim, cycle-accurate), and `hybrid`
(QEMU fast-forwards the boot, vsim measures your region of interest).

## Prerequisites

- An `andesim` checkout, already built (`bash scripts/build_all.sh`).
  Check it with `./andesim doctor`.
- An Andes RISC-V toolchain (the one `doctor` reports).

## Step 1: Modify `Make.var`

Fill in these settings if your paths differ:

```Makefile
ANDESIM ?=            # path to the andesim checkout
TOOLCHAIN_PREFIX ?=   # e.g. .../bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-
ENGINE ?=             # cycle-accurate engine, see `andesim list engines`
```

## Step 2: Build

```bash
make
```

Each demo links against the andesim runtime
(`-B $(ANDESIM)/build/runtime -specs=andesim.specs`), so the same binary
runs on every mode -- no per-engine builds, no semihosting.

## Step 3: Run

Run every mode of one demo:

```bash
make run-hello
make run-lm
make run-lm_slave
make run-lm_dma
make run-hvm_slave
make run-hvm_dma
make run-rvv
make run-fp
make run-cache
make run-verify
make run-syscall
make run-coremark
make run-dhrystone
```

Or one mode at a time (the `lm-*` / `lm_slave-*` / `lm_dma-*`,
`hvm_slave-*` / `hvm_dma-*`, `rvv-*`, `fp-*`, `cache-*`, `verify-*`,
`syscall-*`, `coremark-*` and `dhrystone-*` targets work the same way):

| Target                     | What it shows                                          |
|----------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|
| `make hello-fast`          | QEMU only: program output, full speed, no cycle figure |
| `make hello-cycle`         | vsim from reset: program output + cycle figure         |
| `make hello-hybrid-marker` | hybrid, ROI marked in source with `<andesim/ROI.h>`    |
| `make hello-hybrid-pc`     | hybrid, same ROI named by symbols (`--pc-start`/`--pc-end`), no markers needed |

`demo/lm` proves the hybrid handoff migrates QEMU data into vsim: the
QEMU phase fills the DLM with a runtime-computed pattern and assembles a
small function into the ILM (through the hart-local view -- both live
outside normal RAM), and the vsim ROI executes the ILM function and
checks every DLM word. `LM_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
On `lm-fast`, plain QEMU knows no engine geometry, so the target passes
the ILM/DLM sizes itself with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/lm_slave` proves the slave-port routing on top of that: the same
SRAMs are also visible at the bus apertures (hart 0 ILM `0xA0000000`,
DLM `0xA0200000`). The QEMU phase writes everything THROUGH the
slave-port view; the vsim ROI reads it back through the slave-port view
(each load goes out the bus master port and back in through the local
memory's slave port). `SLV_OK` means both views alias one SRAM on both
engines and the content crossed the handoff.

`demo/lm_dma` makes the writer a real second master: the ATCDMAC300 DMA
controller copies the pattern from DRAM into the DLM slave-port
aperture during the QEMU phase, and the CPU verifies it inside the vsim
ROI. It has NO cycle target -- the vsim RTL models no DMA controller.
That is the demo's point: with hybrid, setup code may use QEMU's device
models, while the measured ROI needs only the CPU; the DMA-written
bytes still reach the RTL's DLM SRAM through the sidecar transport.

The `hvm` demos repeat the slave-port and DMA tests for the HVM, the
vector unit's 256 KB high-bandwidth memory at `0x90000000` (2 banks, no
enable CSR). Unlike the ILM/DLM the HVM has no hart-local address --
its one window IS the bus subordinate port -- so there is no local-view
demo:

- `demo/hvm_slave` fills the HVM in the QEMU phase and reads it back in
  the vsim ROI (sampled, plus the bank-boundary words); on the RTL each
  access leaves the hart's bus master port and enters the HVM through
  its subordinate port -- the same port an external master uses.
  `HVM_SLV_OK` means the content crossed the handoff.
- `demo/hvm_dma` makes that external master real: the ATCDMAC300 copies
  the pattern from DRAM into the HVM during the QEMU phase; like
  `demo/lm_dma` it has no cycle target.

On the `*-fast` targets, plain QEMU's compiled-in HVM is 1 byte, so
each target passes the real size itself (`hvm_size_pow_2=18`, log2 of
256 KB) with `-global` after `--`.

`demo/rvv` tests the vector unit: the ROI runs an RVV-intrinsic kernel
(`<riscv_vector.h>`, strip-mined by `vsetvl` so any VLEN works); the
workload is an 8x8x8 int32 GEMM. The QEMU phase stages A/B and a scalar
reference; the vsim ROI computes C = A x B on the vector unit and
compares. `RVV_OK` means the intrinsic kernel ran right after the
handoff, with no V setup code inside the ROI. It is built with
`-march=rv64gcv` (the intrinsics need V in the arch string). The kernel
is integer on purpose: this engine's VPU is integer-only, so a
vector-float op (e.g. `vfmacc.vf`) traps on the RTL even though QEMU
accepts it.

`demo/fp` covers the scalar FPU's state, `fcsr`, the way `demo/rvv`
covers the vector unit. The QEMU phase clears `fflags`, sets the
rounding mode to RTZ (the reset default is RNE) and raises the sticky
divide-by-zero flag with a real `1.0f/0.0f`; the vsim ROI computes
`1.0f/3.0f` -- a quotient that rounds DIFFERENTLY under RTZ
(`0x3eaaaaaa`) and RNE (`0x3eaaaaab`) -- then reads the CSRs back.
`FP_OK` means the transported `frm` steered a real divide after the
handoff (not just a CSR readback), the pre-handoff DZ flag is still
sticky, and the divide's own NX landed on top of it: `fcsr` crossed
intact.

`demo/cache` prices the config transport: the SAME kernel (4 passes
over a 1 KB volatile array) in two hybrid builds. `cache_on` is the
untouched program -- crt0 enables the L1 caches at boot, and only the
transported `mcache_ctl` makes the vsim ROI run cached, as this
program would on silicon. `cache_off` clears the IC|DC enable bits
before the ROI, so the transported value disables the caches and the
same window runs uncached -- about 4.5k vs 42.5k cycles, a ~9x gap on
this kernel (`make check-cache` asserts ratio > 2x). Without the
transport EVERY hybrid figure would look like `cache_off`: the engine
resets with caches off. The demo also carries the platform-cache MMIO
transport tests (`l2c.elf`/`l3c.elf`, one source): the program stages
patterns in the shared-cache registers (Control policy bits, HPM
Control, way masks) on the QEMU leg and asserts them back FROM THE RTL
inside the ROI, printing `L2C_OK`/`L3C_OK`. Hybrid-only by design, and
engine-gated: check.sh picks the leg matching the engine's CACHE
column (`L2:*` on 45-series, `L3:*` on 46/66) and SKIPs, naming the
RTL config, when it shows `-`. There is no cache_off cycle target on
purpose: disabling the D-cache mid-run on the RTL would strand its
dirty lines (that needs a CCTL flush first); on hybrid the vsim
caches start empty at the restore, so the plain disable is exact.

`demo/verify` is about trusting the figure: `make verify-hybrid-marker`
runs a state-heavy workload (GPR churn, scalar FP under RTZ, an RVV
loop, CSR writes before and inside the ROI) with `--verify`, which
re-runs the same ELF on pure QEMU up to the ROI exit and compares the
drained state field by field against the cycle engine
(`[state-diff] PASS` + `[verify] PASS`). The demo also shows the
failing side: `make verify-taint-hybrid-marker` runs a build whose only
difference is one instruction -- an `mcycle` sample into `t6` right at
the exit marker. The engines count cycles differently by design, so
that register cannot match: verify exits non-zero and the diff names
exactly `x31`. `make check-verify` asserts both directions.

`demo/syscall` exercises the runtime's syscall channels with one
binary: stdout (UART), file io and `gettimeofday()` (HTIF, served
host-side -- `fopen`/`fread` hit real files in the working directory),
and the exit code (SimControl). The QEMU phase writes a
time-of-day-seeded payload to a host file and CLOSES it; the vsim ROI
runs a `printf`, reopens and reads the file back, and removes it.
`SYSCALL_OK` means both legs talked to the same host filesystem. It
also shows the two hybrid rules: close files before the handoff (host
file descriptors live in the engine process and do not cross -- closed
files do), and put must-run code inside the ROI (a hybrid run ends at
the exit trigger, so nothing after the ROI executes; the pass signal on
hybrid is the printed `SYSCALL_OK`, while fast and cycle also check
main's return value through SimControl).

`demo/coremark` runs a real benchmark, EEMBC CoreMark, with the EEMBC
sources untouched: the ROI markers live in the port layer
(`core_portme.c`), inside `start_time()` and `stop_time()` -- the two
functions that already delimit the timed run -- so the hybrid window is
exactly the region CoreMark times itself with its own `mcycle` reads.
That makes the modes cross-check each other: cycle mode's self-reported
`Total ticks` and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region and agree within ~0.5% (the hybrid window starts with cold
caches and includes the marker/call boundary). The pc-trigger variant
gets the same window from the symbols alone
(`--pc-start start_time --pc-end stop_time`). On hybrid the run ends at
`stop_time()`'s exit marker, so CoreMark's report (CRCs, validation)
prints on fast and cycle only; the hybrid output is just the cycle
figure. `ITERATIONS=1` by default -- the CRCs still validate, and each
extra iteration adds RTL simulation time.

`demo/dhrystone` applies the same recipe to Dhrystone 2.2a (the vsim
port, which times with `mcycle`/`minstret` instead of UNIX time APIs):
the counter reads moved into `start_time()`/`stop_time()`, which carry
the ROI markers outside the reads and double as the
`--pc-start`/`--pc-end` symbols. The guest's self-reported `CycleCnt`
(cycle mode) and the hybrid `[andesim] N cycles` figure measure the
same region; on hybrid the run ends at `stop_time()`'s marker, so the
`InstCnt/CycleCnt` line prints on fast and cycle only. `RUNS=1000` by
default (`make dhrystone-cycle RUNS=100` for a quicker RTL run); note
Dhrystone keeps the two-pass compile rule (`dry.c` builds twice, the
second pass with `-DPASS2`).

Expected output (hybrid):

```
hello from andesim!
[andesim] 3532 cycles
```

The two hybrid runs measure the same window, so their cycle figures are
close; the small gap is the marker HINTs and boundary placement.

## Switching engines

Every `cycle` and `hybrid` target takes its engine from the `ENGINE`
variable (default in `Make.var`), so any demo runs on any engine that
`andesim list engines` reports -- the binaries are engine-portable:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced
make check ENGINE=vsim:ax46mpv_advanced        # the whole suite, one engine
make check-all-engines                          # the whole suite, EVERY vsim engine
```

`check-all-engines` parses the engine set from `andesim list engines`
at run time (nothing hardcoded; restrict it with
`SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b"`) and prints a per-engine summary.
Demos are capability-gated per engine: the local-memory demos
(`lm*`, `hvm*`) are skipped on an engine whose resolved plan carries
no ILM/DLM/HVM, and `rvv` is skipped on an engine without a vector
unit. The gate keys off the engine's `--describe` output, which
advertises LM *transport* (backdoor load + dump in the vsim CPU
wrapper) -- not whether the RTL config has the memories.

### Demo x engine matrix (sweep of 2026-07-14)

| Demo      | vsim:ax45mpv_premium | vsim:ax46mpv_advanced | vsim:ax66_makatau | Blocking layer for SKIP/FAIL |
|-----------|----------------------|-----------------------|-------------------|------------------------------|
| hello     | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| lm        | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| lm_slave  | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| lm_dma    | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no ILM/DLM |
| hvm_slave | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
| hvm_dma   | PASS | PASS | SKIP | RTL: ax66 has no HVM |
| rvv       | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| fp        | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cache     | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| cache/l2c+l3c | SKIP | SKIP | PASS (L3C) | RTL: ax45/ax46 built with `NDS_L2C/L3C_CACHE_SIZE_KB=0` (no shared-cache block); wrapper+driver transport ready |
| verify    | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| syscall   | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| coremark  | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| dhrystone | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |
| memsize   | PASS | PASS | PASS | - |

The cache/l2c+l3c row is the platform-cache MMIO transport leg inside
`make check-cache` (sweep of 2026-07-15). The shared cache is the L2C
on 45-series engines and the L3C on 46/66-series -- separate tests,
same registers: `l3c.elf` passes on ax66_makatau's live 512K L3C
(`andesim list engines` CACHE column `L3:512K`); ax45mpv_premium and
ax46mpv_advanced are RTL-blocked (size 0 in their engine cfgs, and
their current RTL drops do not support a shared-cache configuration),
so the leg SKIPs there naming that layer. When an RTL drop with the
block arrives, the leg starts running by itself: the gate is
`--describe`-driven, so no wrapper, driver, or demo change is needed.

The ax66 lm*/hvm* SKIPs are RTL-layer, not a wrapper transport gap:
`vsim_andesim/data/configs/ax66_makatau.cfg` sets
`NDS_ILM_SUPPORT no`, `NDS_DLM_SUPPORT no` (sizes 0) and has no HVM
section at all -- `--describe`'s `ilm_size/dlm_size/hvm_size: 0` is
the wrapper reporting that truthfully. (Contrast with the ax46 history
below, where the RTL HAD the memories and the wrapper was the gap.)

demo/syscall FAILED on ax66 in earlier sweeps: the legacy HTIF
protocol staged syscall args/results in cacheable RAM which the vsim
host peeked/poked by backdoor -- invisible through ax66's private
write-back PL2C, so the guest read its own stale line back
(`SYSCALL_STAGE_BAD gettimeofday`). Fixed on 2026-07-14 by moving the
mailbox into an uncached SimControl device window (coherent by
construction on every cache hierarchy; `flush_dcache()` deleted from
the runtime). Contract + evidence: `andesim/ROADMAP_HTIF_WINDOW.md`;
commits vsim_andesim `c90c234`, qemu fork `2342ca8227`, andesim
`0e3a13e`.

The lm*/hvm* rows were SKIP on ax46mpv_advanced until vsim_andesim
commit 29f6dbf: the RTL config always had the memories, but the CPU
wrapper lacked the set_/get_ backdoor pair, so `--describe` advertised
size 0 and the driver armed no sidecars.

Not in this sweep: `vsim:d23` (rv32; the demos are rv64 builds),
`qemu*` (the sweep covers rv64 vsim engines only).

## Debugging a failed run

Use andesim's logs -- they are designed to locate the problem:

```bash
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 1"   # + per-leg detail
make hello-hybrid-marker ANDESIM_FLAGS="--log-level 0 --log-file run.log"
```

- `--log-level` uses vsim's scale: 0=trace 1=debug 2=info (default)
  3=warn 4=error 5=critical 6=off.
- On a hybrid failure andesim keeps a repro bundle (state files, exact
  commands, manifest) under `~/.cache/andesim/repro/` and prints its path.

## Layout

```
Make.var        shared configuration (paths, toolchain, engine)
Makefile        builds and runs every demo below
demo/hello/     hello world on all four modes
demo/lm/        ILM/DLM content transport across the hybrid handoff
demo/lm_slave/  the same SRAMs through the bus slave-port apertures
demo/lm_dma/    a DMA master fills the DLM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/hvm_slave/ HVM content transport through the bus subordinate port
demo/hvm_dma/   a DMA master fills the HVM, the CPU reads it in the ROI
demo/rvv/       RVV-intrinsic kernel (8x8x8 GEMM) inside the ROI
demo/fp/        scalar FP state: frm steers a divide in the ROI, fflags stay sticky
demo/cache/     the mcache_ctl transport, priced: one kernel cached vs uncached
demo/verify/    --verify: the vsim drain vs the QEMU oracle, plus a taint build it must catch
demo/syscall/   stdio, host file io and exit code on every mode
demo/coremark/  EEMBC CoreMark; the ROI is the benchmark's own timed region
demo/dhrystone/ Dhrystone 2.2a; same recipe, two-pass compile kept
```

68	# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
69	# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
70	# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
71	# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
72	check:
73		@fail=""; \
74		for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
75		  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
76		  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
77		    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
78		  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
79		    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
80		  else \
81		    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
82		  fi; \
83		done; \
84		echo "===================================="; \
85		if [ -z "$$fail" ]; then echo "ALL DEMOS OK"; \
86		else echo "FAILED DEMOS:$$fail"; exit 1; fi

90	# engine whose resolved hybrid plan (--dry-run) carries no ILM/DLM/HVM
91	# sidecar args, or whose `list engines` row shows no VLEN.

94	NEED_V   := demo/rvv demo/verify

97	# is parsed from `andesim list engines` at run time (rv64 rows; the demos
98	# are rv64 builds). Restrict it with SWEEP_ENGINES="vsim:a vsim:b". Fails if
99	# any engine fails any demo it is capable of.
100	check-all-engines:
101		@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \
102		if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
103		  engines=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
104		             | awk '$$2 == "vsim" && $$4 == 64 { print $$1 }'); \
105		fi; \
106		if [ -z "$$engines" ]; then \
107		  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
108		fi; \
109		$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
110		summary=""; bad=""; \

112		  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
113		          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
114		  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \

           demo/hvm_slave demo/hvm_dma demo/rvv demo/fp demo/cache \
           demo/verify demo/syscall demo/coremark demo/dhrystone demo/memsize

RUN_TARGETS := $(patsubst demo/%,run-%,$(SUBDIRS))

# RUN_TARGETS are deliberately NOT .PHONY: make never matches pattern
# rules (run-%) against .PHONY targets.
.PHONY: all run check check-all-engines clean $(SUBDIRS)

all: $(SUBDIRS)

$(SUBDIRS):
	$(MAKE) -C $@

run: $(RUN_TARGETS)

run-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/$* run

# Forward per-mode targets, e.g. `make hello-fast` -> demo/hello hello-fast.
hello-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello $@

lm-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm $@

lm_slave-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_slave $@

lm_dma-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/lm_dma $@

hvm_slave-%:

rvv-%:

cache-%:

verify-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/verify $@

syscall-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/syscall $@

coremark-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/coremark $@

dhrystone-%:
	$(MAKE) -C demo/dhrystone $@

memsize-%:

# Aggregate check: every demo that defines its own `check` runs it (real
# asserts); the rest are asserted to `run` cleanly (exit 0) across all modes.
# Continues past failures and reports a summary. Heavy -- coremark/dhrystone
# run their full cycle/hybrid legs. For one demo use `make check-<name>`.
check:
	@fail=""; \
	for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	  echo "########## $$dir ##########"; \
	  if $(MAKE) -C $$dir -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	    $(MAKE) -C $$dir check || fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  elif $(MAKE) -C $$dir run; then \
	    echo "[PASS] $$dir: run exits 0 (no asserts)"; \
	  else \
	    echo "[FAIL] $$dir: run failed"; fail="$$fail $$dir"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "===================================="; \

check-all-engines:
	@engines="$(SWEEP_ENGINES)"; \

	  echo "no rv64 vsim engine installed (see: andesim list engines)"; exit 1; \
	fi; \
	$(MAKE) -C demo/hello hello.elf >/dev/null; \
	summary=""; bad=""; \
	for eng in $$engines; do \
	  plan=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" run --mode hybrid --trigger marker \
	          --engine "$$eng" --dry-run demo/hello/hello.elf </dev/null 2>&1); \
	  vlen=$$("$(ANDESIM_BIN)" list engines 2>/dev/null \
	          | awk -v e="$$eng" '$$1 == e { print $$5 }'); \
	  skips=""; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "ilm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_LM)"; \
	  echo "$$plan" | grep -q "hvm_size=[1-9]" || skips="$$skips $(NEED_HVM)"; \
	  case "$$vlen" in ""|-|0) skips="$$skips $(NEED_V)";; esac; \
	  dirs=""; \
	  for d in $(SUBDIRS); do \
	    case " $$skips " in *" $$d "*) ;; *) dirs="$$dirs $$d";; esac; \
	  done; \
	  echo "#################### ENGINE $$eng ####################"; \
	  if [ -n "$$skips" ]; then echo "[SKIP] $$eng lacks the hardware for:$$skips"; fi; \
	  if $(MAKE) check ENGINE="$$eng" SUBDIRS="$$dirs"; then \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: OK (skipped:$${skips:- none})"; \
	  else \
	    summary="$$summary\n  $$eng: FAILED"; bad="$$bad $$eng"; \
	  fi; \
	done; \
	echo "#################### ENGINE SWEEP ####################"; \
	printf "engines:$$summary\n"; \
	if [ -n "$$bad" ]; then echo "FAILED ENGINES:$$bad"; exit 1; fi

# Single demo: its own `check` if defined, else assert `run` exits 0.
check-%:
	@if $(MAKE) -C demo/$* -n check >/dev/null 2>&1; then \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* check; \
	else \
	  echo "demo/$*: no asserts -- running to assert exit 0"; \
	  $(MAKE) -C demo/$* run; \
	fi

clean:
	@for dir in $(SUBDIRS); do $(MAKE) -C $$dir clean; done

## 14. cpp

State: DONE (2026-07-15)
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `cpp`.

C++ on the andesim runtime, unblocked and demoed. Runtime side (andesim
commit `946e2e3`, TDD'd by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`, 12/12 vplat
scripts green): crt0 keeps the direct `init_mtvec` call (that name
reference is what extracts handler.o from `libandesim_runtime.a`, and
the trap vector is live before any ctor) then walks `.init_array` via
newlib's `__libc_init_array`; `andesim.ld` PROVIDEs the array bounds
ABOVE `_edata` -- crt0 zeroes `[_edata, _end)` before the walk, so
arrays after `.data` would be wiped; `andesim.specs` adds
crtbegin/crtend (the g++ driver injects `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, so *lib
is untouched); main's return routes through `exit()` (C++
return-from-main == exit(rc): atexit + static dtors run). Demo side:
the static ctor assembles the "CPP" tag into a `std::string` before
main; the vsim ROI re-checks the tag from the RTL (the object's bytes
crossed the handoff), grows a `std::vector` on the newlib heap and
prints the runtime-composed `CPP_OK` inside the ROI; `CPP_DTOR_OK`
prints after main returns (fast/cycle only -- hybrid ends at the exit
marker). The ROI kernel is `extern "C"`: the pc trigger resolves
symbols by name, so `cpp_roi`/`cpp_roi_end` must stay unmangled.
PASS on all four legs x all three engines (see README matrix).

- Key files: `demo/cpp/{main.cpp,Makefile}`, `Make.var` (adds CXX), top
  `Makefile`, `README.md`; andesim `runtime/{crt0.S,handler.c,andesim.ld,
  andesim.specs}` + `tests/fixtures/vplat_cpp.cpp` +
  `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh` + USER_GUIDE 4.1 (other repo).
- Pass: guest prints `CPP_OK` composed by the static ctor inside the
  ROI on every mode; `CPP_DTOR_OK` + exit 0 on fast/cycle.
- Deps: none (runtime change landed).

## 14. cpp

State: DONE (2026-07-15)
Modes: fast, cycle, hybrid (marker + pc).
Origin: vsim-demo-new `cpp`.

C++ on the andesim runtime, unblocked and demoed. Runtime side (andesim
commit `946e2e3`, TDD'd by `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`, 12/12 vplat
scripts green): crt0 keeps the direct `init_mtvec` call (that name
reference is what extracts handler.o from `libandesim_runtime.a`, and
the trap vector is live before any ctor) then walks `.init_array` via
newlib's `__libc_init_array`; `andesim.ld` PROVIDEs the array bounds
ABOVE `_edata` -- crt0 zeroes `[_edata, _end)` before the walk, so
arrays after `.data` would be wiped; `andesim.specs` adds
crtbegin/crtend (the g++ driver injects `-lstdc++ -lm` itself, so *lib
is untouched); main's return routes through `exit()` (C++
return-from-main == exit(rc): atexit + static dtors run). Demo side:
the static ctor assembles the "CPP" tag into a `std::string` before
main; the vsim ROI re-checks the tag from the RTL (the object's bytes
crossed the handoff), grows a `std::vector` on the newlib heap and
prints the runtime-composed `CPP_OK` inside the ROI; `CPP_DTOR_OK`
prints after main returns (fast/cycle only -- hybrid ends at the exit
marker). The ROI kernel is `extern "C"`: the pc trigger resolves
symbols by name, so `cpp_roi`/`cpp_roi_end` must stay unmangled.
PASS on all four legs x all three engines (see README matrix).

- Key files: `demo/cpp/{main.cpp,Makefile}`, `Make.var` (adds CXX), top
  `Makefile`, `README.md`; andesim `runtime/{crt0.S,handler.c,andesim.ld,
  andesim.specs}` + `tests/fixtures/vplat_cpp.cpp` +
  `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh` + USER_GUIDE 4.1 (other repo).
- Pass: guest prints `CPP_OK` composed by the static ctor inside the
  ROI on every mode; `CPP_DTOR_OK` + exit 0 on fast/cycle.
- Deps: none (runtime change landed).

ROADMAP entry 14 is DONE: C++ works on the andesim runtime, and `demo/cpp` proves it on every mode and engine.

**What landed**

andesim repo (`946e2e3`, TDD - the new test failed first with "CPP_FAIL static ctor did not run"):
- `runtime/andesim.ld`: kept `.preinit_array/.init_array/.fini_array` with `PROVIDE_HIDDEN` bounds, plus `.eh_frame`. Placed above `_edata` on purpose - crt0 zeroes `[_edata, _end)` before the walk, so arrays after `.data` would be wiped.
- `runtime/crt0.S`: keeps the direct `init_mtvec` call (that name reference is what extracts handler.o from the archive, and the trap vector is live before any ctor), then calls newlib's `__libc_init_array`; main's return now routes through `exit()` so atexit + static dtors run (C++ return-from-main semantics).
- `runtime/andesim.specs`: startfile/endfile gain `crtbegin/crtend`; `*lib` untouched because the g++ driver injects `-lstdc++ -lm` itself.
- New regression guard: `tests/fixtures/vplat_cpp.cpp` + `tests/vplat/test_vplat_cpp.sh`; all 12 vplat scripts pass. USER_GUIDE 4.1 documents the g++ command.

demo repo (`2f11908` + study-entries docs commit `18e3a40`):
- `demo/cpp`: static ctor assembles "CPP" into a `std::string` before main; the vsim ROI re-checks the tag from the RTL side (the object crossed the handoff), grows a `std::vector` on the newlib heap, prints `CPP_OK` inside the ROI; `CPP_DTOR_OK` prints at exit on fast/cycle. One gotcha worth knowing: the pc trigger resolves symbols by name, so the ROI kernel is `extern "C"` (mangled `_Z7cpp_roiv` was "not defined").
- `Make.var` adds `CXX`; top Makefile, README section + layout + matrix row.

**Evidence**

| cpp leg | ax45mpv_premium | ax46mpv_advanced | ax66_makatau |
|---|---|---|---|
| fast | PASS | PASS | PASS |
| cycle | PASS (11654 cyc) | PASS (9291) | PASS (11961) |
| hybrid-marker | PASS (5787) | PASS (4505) | PASS (5913) |
| hybrid-pc | PASS (5773) | PASS (4501) | PASS (5913) |

Regression on the relinked runtime: `make check` across the 13 non-benchmark demos = **ALL DEMOS OK** (cache 9.4x ratio intact, verify passes and still catches the taint, memsize matrix green), plus `coremark-fast` (CRC validated) and `dhrystone-fast`. The two benchmark cycle/hybrid legs were skipped as the documented long-running exclusion; their boot-time-only crt0 delta doesn't touch the measured window.
